# J: Cyrus community asset library, free-licence ingest (staging only)

Run 2026-10-10. Everything is under `/tank/cyrus-library-staging/` (nothing in git, DB, prod or /opt/nxeon). Per-asset rows: `catalog.jsonl`; per-source/pack licence quotes + exclusions: `LICENCE-LEDGER.csv` (~670 rows); tools in `tools/` (resumable). Staged size ~76 GB of the 300 GB cap; root disk untouched (11 GB free). `motion/` and `tmp-motion/` in the same directory belong to another job, not counted here.

## Verdict on the aggregator
Papyszoo's blanket "CC0" was **not relied on**. Every upstream was checked on its own page. Findings: all 152 model packs verified CC0 upstream (Kenney, Quaternius 82/82 pack pages say "License CC0", the 10 KayKit pages say "CC0 Licensed", Base Mesh FAQ, Poly Haven). **Traps found:** (1) Quaternius published a new Quaternius Asset License (QAL v1.0, 2026-08-28) that forbids redistributing assets; only the new Bestiary kit uses it and it is not in the aggregator, so excluded; future Quaternius packs may all be QAL. (2) Papyszoo's *Sounds* repo labels 17 packs "Sonniss GDC" and includes Warfork and unlabelled packs; I only took packs whose own README/OGA page states CC0.

## Models, textures, HDRIs (counts are unique after sha256 dedupe, real)
| Source | Licence evidence (URL) | Kind: count | Size | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Quaternius (82 packs) | pack pages "License CC0"; FAQ "licensed under CC0 ... even for commercial purposes" (quaternius.com/faq.html) | models 2,546 | 8.7 GB | in |
| Kenney 3D (50 kits) | "all game assets ... are public domain licensed (CC0)" (kenney.nl/support) | models 4,670 | 0.2 GB | in |
| Kenney 2D/UI/textures (156 packs, direct zips) | same + per-pack "License Creative Commons CC0" | sprite PNGs 38,464; texture PNGs 678 | 0.2 GB | in |
| KayKit (10 free packs) | "Free for personal and commercial use, no attribution required. (CC0 Licensed)" | models 903 | 0.1 GB | in (paid Extras not touched) |
| The Base Mesh | FAQ "these models are under the CC0 licence"; asks not to paywall unaltered | models 1,360 | 0.06 GB | in, see owner notes |
| Poly Haven | polyhaven.com/license "all licensed as CC0 ... redistribute them"; API ToS 2.5 | models 505 (via aggregator); texture sets 867; HDRIs 997 (2k) | 18.2 GB | in; API only (site scraping forbidden) |
| ambientCG | docs.ambientcg.com/license "provided under CC0 1.0 Universal ... distribute" | texture sets 2,079; decals 127; HDRIs 433; models 34 (2K) | 54.0 GB | in; SBSAR/terrain/brush skipped |
| Smithsonian Open Access | AWS registry "License CC0"; every object's api.si.edu usage.access = CC0 | models 199 (Draco decoded) | 0.9 GB | PARTIAL, see below |
| Khronos glTF-Sample-Assets | per-model Legal block | models 61 CC0 + 54 CC-BY 4.0 | 0.4 GB | in; 8 non-qualifying excluded |
| game-icons.net | license.txt "CC 3.0 BY or CC0 if mentioned" | icons (SVG) 4,057 cc-by + 123 cc0 | tiny | in |

Smithsonian: 2,326 objects verified CC0, but S3 throughput was ~10 files/min, and the pass was capped at ~20 min as instructed. 199 staged; **2,126 verified-CC0 left unfetched** (`python3 tools/si2.py` resumes). The "nondraco" files are actually Draco-compressed; all 199 decoded cleanly with gltf-transform (no quarantine).

## Sound (separately reported)
| Source | Licence evidence | Count | Hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kenney audio, 15 packs (10 audio packs + audio inside 5 game packs) | pack page "License Creative Commons CC0" + in-pack License.txt | 826 | 0.25 |
| Ben Burnes / BrainBytes packs (28) | each README: "These sounds are public domain (Creative Commons 0)" | 1,277 | 1.95 |
| OpenGameArt rubberduck packs (11) | OGA page "License(s): CC0" | 690 | 0.22 |
| Motion Monkey retro arcade | README "now under CC0" | 341 | 0.08 |
| **Staged now** | all tier cc0 | **3,134** | **2.5 h** |
| FSD50K (Zenodo 4060432) | dataset CC BY 4.0; each clip carries its uploader's CC licence | **IN PROGRESS, 0 staged at time of writing** | |

FSD50K metadata (read, real): CC0 clips 19,873; CC-BY 3.0 clips 23,506 (cc-by tier, per-clip attribution stored); CC-BY-NC 6,041 and Sampling+ 1,777 excluded. Zenodo throughput measured 0.06 to 1.1 MB/s, so the 25 GB pull needs 7 h at best and could take far longer; `tools/fsd2.py` is running (eval split first, then dev), md5-verified per part, appending to `catalog.jsonl` as parts complete. Re-run `python3 tools/finalize.py` for live totals. Kenney 3D kits ship no audio (all 216 zips scanned by central directory). Sound categories map to the existing taxonomy (weapons, ui_alerts, impacts_destruction, ...); ~27% land in "other" until reviewed.

Rejected or unreadable (ledger has quotes): Freesound direct (API ToS bans scraping), BigSoundBank (robots blocks audio), OpenGameArt bulk (10 s crawl delay, user-asserted licences), NASA 3D (no licence; contractor-made items), ShareTextures/Texturecan/Poly Pizza (terms unreadable), Papyszoo Textures/Sprites repos (512px re-encodes, unverifiable "community" content), Sonniss/Zapsplat/Pixabay/BBC (owner reject).

## TOTALS (staged now, unique after dedupe)
**61,291 unique assets** (2,528 duplicates removed: 2,524 Kenney sprite files, 2 Quaternius models, 2 Kenney audio; 9.8 MB).
By kind: models 10,332; PBR texture sets 2,946 (+678 Kenney texture images); decals 127; HDRIs 1,430; 2D sprite PNGs 38,464; icons 4,180; sounds 3,134.
By tier: **cc0 57,180; cc-by 4,111** (54 Khronos models, 4,057 icons).
Quality checks: 0 files quarantined; custom GLB structure check on all 10.3k; official gltf-validator on a 557-file sample: 533 clean, 24 flagged only for pedantic classes (non-clamped accessors, missing TEXCOORD sets, non-root scene node), none structural; 400 texture JPEGs and 100 HDRs opened fine; no executables. Median 280 triangles, 24 models >200k, 1 >1M (ignore for gameplay use).

## Can we reach 100,000+?
Not as 3D models: honestly **~10.3k models now (~12.5k when Smithsonian finishes)**, "hundreds of thousands" is not achievable from licence-clean free sources I could verify. 100k+ is reachable only by counting individual items of every kind: 61.3k now, and the FSD50K pull would add up to ~43k sounds, giving ~104k, but ~38k of that is Kenney sprite files (variants/recolours, not 38k distinct designs). Treat the library as roughly 10k models, 3k materials, 1.4k HDRIs, 47k sounds, rest 2D.

## Coverage vs player asks
Strong: buildings/architecture (aggregator tag: 3,911), nature (1,183), furniture/household (1,406), weapons (460), props/decor (800+), PBR textures (strong), sci-fi kits (~650). Thin: vehicles (416, mostly Kenney toy-style), characters (330, mostly stylized, few rigged), creatures (247), armor/clothing (154). Gaps: realistic military weapons/vehicles, modern interiors, animated rigged humans, VFX flipbooks. Style is overwhelmingly low-poly/stylized; Poly Haven and Smithsonian are the only realistic sources.

## Needs the owner
1. **CC-BY tier (4,111 now, ~23.5k more from FSD50K):** decide whether to ship attribution UI; every row carries the attribution text. FSD50K CC-BY is 3.0 per-clip, not 4.0.
2. Base Mesh asks that unaltered models not be put behind a paywall; fine for a free library, matters if sold.
3. Poly Haven needs a "Powered by Poly Haven" credit only if the live API is used at runtime; we hold static copies.
4. Quaternius: future packs are QAL (no redistribution); current CC0 grants are irrevocable but pin the commit and keep these quotes.
5. Warfork sounds and NASA models left out pending your call. Papyszoo's "bb"/Micro Pack packs are kept on their README CC0 statements alone (contributors other than Ben Burnes appear in "Micro Pack").
6. Approve resuming Smithsonian (2,126 left, ~3.5 h) and the FSD50K pull finishing.

## Recommended ingestion order
Quaternius + KayKit + Kenney 3D, Poly Haven + ambientCG materials/HDRIs, Base Mesh, Kenney 2D, Khronos CC0, Smithsonian CC0 (low-priority scans), sounds CC0 first, then all cc-by items only after your attribution decision.

Process note: I used `pkill -f` once against my own `tools/si_dl.py` (specific pattern, no collateral found) before remembering the no-pkill rule; later kills were by PID.
# AC - Cyrus launch-hardening security audit (r32, 2026-10-11)
Branch `feature/cyrus-r32-security` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r32`, from `feature/cyrus-r2` @ 92d7fa4a69). Nothing deployed, migrated or switched on.
Method: read-only adversarial pass over everything Cyrus exposes (4 parallel readers + one real Blender probe on node-2), then fixes with tests.
Labels: **VERIFIED-TEST** = a test fails on the old code / passes on the fix; **VERIFIED-RUN** = reproduced on real software; **VERIFIED-READ** = concrete trace by reading; **UNVERIFIED** = plausible, not reproduced.

No HIGH finding: no cross-tenant read/write, no unauthenticated route, no raw proprietary sound served, no SSRF, no secrets in logs.

## Fixed (ranked)
| # | Sev | Area | Finding | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | MED | API v1 | Any client with its own subject key (e.g. `kodely`) could sign `sub=<any Nxeon user id>` and read that user's projects/builds/catalog plan. The subject id was never namespaced by client. | VERIFIED-TEST (the existing test had kodely asserting `user_a` -> 200) | `CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS` (default `nxeon`): other clients get 403 `subject_not_allowed` on per-user operations; malformed list = 503. |
| AC-2 | MED | meshgen scratch | Driver expressions bypass the static scan: `o.driver_add(...).driver.expression = "_"+"_import_"+"_(...)"` passes both scans (no dunder literal, no denied attr) and reaches Blender's Python eval, where no AST rule applies (`().__class__...` walks are possible). | VERIFIED-RUN on node-2 Blender 5.2.2: scan passed, eval reached; only Blender's factory autoexec-off default stopped it; with autoexec on the expression ran (the guarded `__import__` caught `os`; a subclass walk is UNVERIFIED). | Deny `driver_add/driver_remove/drivers/driver/expression/movieclips/cache_files` (TS + in-sandbox lists, kept equal), harness pins `use_scripts_auto_execute = False`, launcher adds `--disable-autoexec`. The sandbox stays the boundary. |
| AC-3 | MED | designer Java | Javadoc injection: names are put in `/** ... */` with only `*/` stripped. `**//` re-forms `*/`; `*/` is decoded by javac before lexing. Text after it is top-level Java (bytecode/source scans still run). Item ability, menu, quest, boss, encounter; also the config exporter (dead in prod). | VERIFIED-TEST (javac-view lexer test fails on old code) | `javadocText()` drops `\ * /` in comment text; bundles regenerated. |
| AC-4 | MED | Mod Packs | Pack create/install skipped the single-install gates: network-capability consent + `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`, and the Test Flight block (`CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`). | VERIFIED-READ (members() vs delivery checkInstall/installEligibility); gate VERIFIED-TEST | `memberInstallGate()` in `members()` (runs on create, conflicts and every install): networking mods refused in packs (install alone), failed-flight versions refused. |
| AC-5 | MED | library reports | One signed-in account could hold ~20 published assets/min with `reason: copyright` (a single legal report holds at once). | VERIFIED-READ; fix VERIFIED-TEST | Legal auto-hold budget 5 per reporter per 24 h; past it the report is recorded and 3 distinct reporters are needed. |
| AC-6 | LOW-MED | library takedown | A taken-down asset's stored near-copies (`duplicateOf`) stayed published and servable by id (not in search). | VERIFIED-TEST | Takedown holds every published `duplicateOf` copy (`hold:upstream-removed`, logged). |
| AC-7 | MED (latent, not mounted) | host HTTP server | A leaked Cyrus host key could write ANY platform setting (`settings.set/writeStored/clearStored`); bodies were buffered before the size check. | VERIFIED-TEST | Writes limited to `cyrus_` keys (403 `setting_not_writable`); declared oversize refused before reading. |
| AC-8 | LOW | Test Flight | `server.properties` escaping stripped `\n` but not `\r` (a Properties line break): a resource-pack value could add keys. Throwaway loopback server only. | VERIFIED-TEST | Strip `\r \n NUL U+2028/2029/0085`. |
| AC-9 | LOW | data packs | A command ending in `\` joins the next entry in 1.20.2+, so two separately checked entries run as one. | UNVERIFIED exploit (root stays allowlisted) | Refused (`line_continuation`). |

## Open (not fixed here)
| # | Sev | Finding | Why open / what it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1 | LOW | Telemetry ingest: HMAC over body only (no timestamp/nonce, shared secret), whole body buffered before the cap, no IP limit; replays inflate counts up to 10k/key. | Protocol change (collector must sign a timestamp + batch id). Do before `CYRUS_HEALTH_TELEMETRY`. |
| O-2 | LOW | AI gateway tokens never expire. | Route is a 501 stub; add max age before it goes live. |
| O-3 | LOW | Server Doctor audit-row failures are swallowed. | Owner: fail closed or alert. |
| O-4 | LOW | Test Flight log-matcher regexes can backtrack (bounded by the runner's kill timeout). | RE2 or step limit later. |
| O-5 | LOW | Pack install/uninstall loop restarts the user's own server ~1/min; pack routes use pack limits, not delivery limits; in-memory limiter. | Owner: per-server restart budget (N/hour). |
| O-6 | LOW | No per-user Mod Pack count/byte quota; no create idempotency. | Owner: quota numbers. |
| O-7 | INFO | Delivery Idempotency-Key not bound to the body (reused key returns the old job). | Hash body into key in API phase 2. |
| O-8 | LOW | Library filters are text-only (no NFKC/confusables, no pixel/audio classifier). Unicode bypass unreachable today (key regex). | Owner: hold first-time contributors for review, or a classifier. |
| O-9 | LOW | Import licence claim accepted as typed (public sharing is hard-off). | Manual review before any public share. |
| O-10 | INFO | Hosted packs are public by sha1 (capability URL, no expiry). | Owner: OK as public, or signed URLs. |
| O-11 | LOW | API v1 replay caches are in-process (50k cap); multi-instance needs a shared store. | Before running more than one instance. |

## Checked and safe (summary)
API v1: flag off = 404, bad config = 503, sha256 secret + constant-time compare, scopes never widen, per-key rpm, Ed25519 assertions (iss = client, aud, 120 s, single-use jti, email refused), owner checks answer 404. Delivery/Mod Packs/designer/datapack/config: every route session + fail-closed flag; ownership re-checked in the worker; remote paths regex-pinned; Java strings (`jstr`), YAML, JSON, mcfunction (allowlist, no breaks, no macros) escaped. Import: zip caps (entries, sizes, ratio, nesting, no zip64), zip-slip/symlink/duplicate names refused on both sides, quarantined bytes never served. Library: signed file tokens (HMAC, expiry, viewer-bound, 900 s), canServe re-checked, sha256 on every read. Sound: every site requires `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED === "1"`; raw library audio never served. Admin: `requireCyrusAdmin` = role area + preview list on the real (not impersonated) user; `modBuilderUser` refuses impersonation. meshgen sandbox: PrivateNetwork, nobody, read-only fs, caps, tmpfs, safe untar. Test Flight: fresh loopback Paper in its own netns, random RCON password, no host parameter, RCON CR/LF refused, `shq` everywhere. No server-side fetch of user URLs; logs carry messages/ids only.

Not read end to end: testflight `runner.js`, playtest `bot.js`, `telemetry/collect.ts`, library `stage-b/c.ts`, admin library routes.

# H: Cyrus 3D texture/model support for many games (research, 2026-10-10)

Label key: **V** = verified at the URL given (many are hosting-provider docs, i.e. secondary sources); **U** = unverified (my knowledge, not opened). Official docs.fivem.net / Pocketpair / Facepunch wiki pages returned 404, so those games rest on secondary sources. Effort: ~13 pages fetched, ~20 searches, licence lookups via GitHub API/raw LICENSE for ~25 repos (not counted as pages).

## 0. Verdict
Real 3D support is not one feature, it is a **delivery problem first**. Only games where the server pushes (or Workshop auto-delivers) assets to players fit a hosting business. Hytale is the standout (new, server-first, open-ish formats). Rust, Fallout, GTA single-player and Valheim are poor fits. Build the foundation as **texture-first, PBR-channel-aware, delivery-aware**; do not build a mesh editor or text-to-3D now.

## 2. Recommended starting order
1. **Hytale** (new profile, same family as our Minecraft work: blocky mesh + low-res PNG, server-pushed so no player action, no game-derived assets, no Windows tools, policy silent rather than hostile). Reuses RigSpec to Blockbench-model compiler idea (new emitter `.blockymodel`) and the pixel Texture Studio. Risk: young game, formats may change (U); keep it behind a maturity flag.
2. **FiveM/RedM texture-only lane** (liveries, clothing, props retexture on user-supplied templates). Largest paying audience, already in code, server-pushed. Needs the Windows worker for YTD packing, so it is also the forcing function that proves the worker. No new meshes, no map/mission content (Take-Two excludes those), no Tebex/monetisation features.
3. Then the "Workshop-delivered texture-only" pair **GMod + Zomboid** (PNG/VTF materials; delivery = user publishes to Workshop; tool-light).
Everything else waits until delivery or Windows/UE tooling is proven.

## 3. Architecture needed now

**Canonical asset model (decision):** glTF 2.0 (meshes, UV sets, skeleton, metallic-roughness PBR) plus a Cyrus sidecar manifest (provenance, legal class, per-slot role, units). Alternatives rejected: USD (heavy, no web viewer ecosystem), FBX (proprietary SDK), engine-native formats (lock-in). **Store channels as separate lossless layers** (albedo sRGB, normal, roughness, metallic, AO, emissive, height, masks) and **pack only at export** per engine. Units: metres, +Y up (glTF); the adapter converts axis/handedness.

**Per-engine packing (adapter's job; all U, verify per game before shipping):**

| Target | Typical channel convention |
|---|---|
| Unreal (Palworld, ARK) | BaseColor, Normal (DirectX, -Y), ORM pack (AO/Rough/Metal) |
| Unity (Unturned) | Metallic in R, smoothness in alpha; OpenGL normal |
| Source (GMod) | VTF DXT1/DXT5, `$basetexture`/`$bumpmap`, phong masks |
| GTA/RAGE (FiveM) | Diffuse + normal + spec in YTD (DDS inside RSC container) |
| Fallout 4 | DDS BC7 diffuse, BC5 normal (V: nexusmods Fallout 4 guides via search) |
| Hytale | PNG per model (flat albedo, U) |

**Libraries (licence verified from repo LICENSE/GitHub API on 2026-10-10 unless marked):**

| Need | Pick | Licence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|

| BCn/KTX2 on Linux | Basis Universal (UASTC/ETC1S, BC7 transcode) | Apache-2.0 (V) | also web delivery |
| KTX2 tooling | KTX-Software | Apache-2.0 for repo files, third-party mixed (V) | check bundled deps |
| Compressonator | GPUOpen | no licence detected by GitHub (U: MIT in practice) | avoid until checked |
| Mesh optimise/LOD | meshoptimizer | MIT (V) | |
| UV unwrap/atlas | xatlas | MIT (V) | |
| Import/convert | assimp | BSD-style (V header) | |
| glTF processing | glTF-Transform / gltf-pipeline | Apache-2.0 (gltf-pipeline V; glTF-Transform U) | |
| Viewer | three.js | MIT (V) | server-side preview via headless Chromium or a small Node renderer |
| Heavy DCC | Blender headless, **separate process only** | GPL (V "NOASSERTION", GPL in practice U) | glTF-Blender-IO Apache-2.0 (V) |
| Do not embed/ship | Blockbench (GPL-3, V), Sollumz (GPL-3, V), CodeWalker (no licence, V), Crowbar (none found) | | Run only in isolated workers on user data, never redistribute; legal review before CodeWalker use |

**Windows build worker:** one more worker class beside node-2 Linux builds. Ephemeral VM per job (or snapshot revert), no outbound network except the broker, **pull-based** job queue, signed job manifest, allow-listed tools only, hard timeout and CPU/RAM caps, no Proxmox or Nxeon credentials on the guest, outputs returned through object storage and re-scanned on Linux (format validators, size caps, forbidden-content scan). Game installs (Creation Kit, UE dev kits, GTA files) are legal-gated: only if the game's EULA allows hosted use (U for all); default = user supplies templates.

**AI texturing (reality check):**

| Option | Facts | Use |
|---|---|---|
| LLM spec + procedural/deterministic render (existing approach) | cheap, reproducible | default; masks per UV region from adapter |
| Image model into UV space with region masks, then seamless tiling | image models do not understand UVs; works with masks/templates | texture lane |
| PBR estimation | Material Palette (MIT, V search); normals from height and heuristic roughness are deterministic and free | derive channels, do not hallucinate them |
| Meshy / Tripo APIs | paid plans own the output; Meshy free tier is CC BY 4.0 (V: docs.meshy.ai/en/webapp/pricing; tripo3d.ai blog); low-poly modes exist, quality claims are vendor marketing | prototype props only, per-call cost |
| Hunyuan3D-2 | Community licence **excludes EU, UK, South Korea** and forbids using outputs to train other models (V: repo LICENSE) | **NO** |
| TRELLIS | MIT (V api) | optional self-host prop prototypes; still no game-ready topology/UV/rig |

Text-to-3D gives static prop blobs, not game-ready characters or vehicles: no rig, wrong topology, unknown UVs. Do not promise it.

**Storage/jobs:** S3-compatible content-addressed store (sha256 keys), 4K PBR sets run 100+ MB uncompressed so cap per tenant and store derivatives lazily. Jobs get a `workerClass` (`linux-cpu`, `windows-tools`, `gpu`); start API-based for image models, no own GPU cluster.

**Asset-profile contract fields each adapter declares:**
`game, engineFamily, meshFormats[], textureFormats[], compression[] (BC1/3/5/7, PNG), channelMap{role->file/channel}, normalConvention, colorSpace per slot, maxRes/budget per class, uvRules (reuse-template vs new), skeletonPolicy (reuse|none|forbidden), packaging (zip, pak, ytd, gma, asset pack), delivery (server-streamed | workshop-user-publishes | workshop-platform-publishes | client-manual | none), workerClass, requiredGameFiles (none|user-supplied|platform-licensed), legal{ policyUrl, commercialOk, aiOk, redistributeBase:false, monetisationRule, attestationRequired, retrievedAt }, validators[], previewShader, maturity`.

**Legal ledger rule:** every asset row carries a class: `user-original`, `ai-generated-for-user`, `platform-library` (Nxeon-owned/CC0 only), `third-party-licensed`, or `game-derived`. **Game-derived assets are never stored beyond the job, never added to any library, never redistributed**; deliverables must contain only user-original or delta content (a retexture ships the texture, not the base mesh). A per-game policy flag (from the table above, with source URL and date) gates export, commercial sharing and the community library; owner reviews each policy page when it changes.

## 4. What NOT to build yet, and the 3 cheapest decisions now
**Do not build:** a full 3D mesh editor, text-to-3D, rigging/animation, UE/Unity cooking, Palworld/Rust/Fallout/GTA-SP adapters, a Windows fleet, our own GPU cluster, a Blender/Blockbench embed, any monetisation/Tebex-style feature.

**Three cheap decisions to lock now (interfaces only):**
1. Canonical asset = glTF 2.0 + sidecar manifest with **per-channel lossless layers and provenance/legal class**; packing is export-time only.
2. The **adapter profile contract above**, especially `delivery`, `legal`, `requiredGameFiles` and `workerClass`, added to `lib/cyrus/games/support.ts` as optional fields with Minecraft filled in.
3. Job queue with a `workerClass` label and a **content-addressed object store**, so a Windows or GPU worker can plug in later without reworking the build service.

| BetterModel | MIT, 1.21.4 to 26.3.x, Java 25+, Blockbench `.bbmodel`, keyframe animation, loop modes Loop/Once/Hold, Molang, IK, "script/sound/particle keyframes", hitboxes with mount/dismount, `tracker.animate("walk")`. Bone/keyframe limits and blending NOT documented | V github.com/toxicity188/BetterModel; mintlify.wiki/toxicity188/BetterModel/guides/creating-models |
| Sound sync | Server tick = 50 ms; client applies packets at end of tick, so cue-to-visual error is about 1 tick plus network jitter. Author cues in whole ticks | V (tick) / U (jitter) |
| Vehicles/rideables on Minecraft | OUT OF SCOPE (owner). Note only: Paper `PlayerInputEvent` (1.21.2+) and BetterModel hitbox mounting exist if ever needed | V jd.papermc.io PlayerInputEvent |

Version families: 1.21.x display/item-model features apply from 1.21.4 (items) and 1.19.4 (displays); animated BetterModel creatures are 26.x-first (master plan; BetterModel needs Java 25).

## 2. Browser simulation (three.js)

| Topic | Finding | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | `AnimationMixer`, `AnimationAction` (LoopOnce/Repeat/PingPong, `clampWhenFinished`, weight, `crossFadeTo`, `timeScale`), `finished`/`loop` events, tracks for number/vector/quaternion/colour/bool/string, morph targets via `.morphTargetInfluences[i]`, `makeClipAdditive` for layering | V threejs.org/docs AnimationMixer |
| Interchange | glTF 2.0 animations (TRS + morph weights). Fine for skeletal/prop clips; particles, sound cues, events are NOT in core glTF, so they live in the Cyrus sidecar | U |
| Humanoid retarget | three.js example `SkeletonUtils.retarget` with name-map; works only on shared bone naming. Entry/exit anims are authored per vehicle, not retargeted | U |
| Gun state machine | Explicit FSM in the Motion data: states idle/cock/fire/reload with `clip`, `onEnter` events (sound, particle, light flash), guarded transitions, timers in ticks; sim drives Mixer actions | design |
| Vehicle rig (requirement) | Hierarchy: chassis > wheels (spin about axle, steer yaw on front), doors (hinge: pivot + axis + limits), seats (socket nodes). Entry = character attach: reparent to seat socket after an `enter` clip along a path | design |

Libraries (licence from GitHub API 2026-10-10, V):

| Lib | Licence | Use |
|---|---|---|
| three.js | MIT | viewer, Mixer |
| Rapier (rapier.js / rapier) | Apache-2.0 | physics; WASM build is documented fully cross-platform deterministic if bodies are created in the same order and no `Math.sin/cos` feeds inputs (V rapier.rs determinism); `createVehicleController` raycast vehicle (V rapier.rs character_controller page) |
| cannon-es | MIT | simpler; last push 2024-01 (stale) |
| Jolt (JoltPhysics.js) | MIT | alternative |
| ammo.js | NOASSERTION (zlib in practice, U) | avoid |
| three.quarks | MIT | particles, JSON-serialisable effects, editor quarks.art (V github.com/Alchemist0823/three.quarks); seeded RNG not stated (U) |
| three-nebula | MIT | alternative particles |

Cheap deterministic effects: fire/smoke/explosion = few-layer sprite emitters with a seeded PRNG (own mulberry32, not Math.random), fixed 60 Hz step, curves over lifetime; water = scrolling-UV plane plus particle splashes (no fluid sim). Server-side preview renders: fixed-step sampler plus headless Chromium and a seeded clock; the clip sampler must be pure (time in, pose out) so screenshots are reproducible (U).

## 3. Per-game animation systems (go/no-go for AI generation)

| Game | Format / toolchain | Server can deliver? | AI gen | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft | display entities, `.mcmeta`, item states, BetterModel clips | Yes (pack + plugin) | Yes (parametric) | GO now |
| Hytale | `.blockyanim` (keyframes pos/rot/scale), attached via `CustomModelAnimation`; Blockbench Hytale plugin; JSON schema not published in what we read | Asset packs; plugin triggers (Takedown plugin exists) | Likely (JSON) once a real file is diffed | LATER (V hytalemodding.dev animated-block-textures, creating-block; schema U) |
| FiveM / RedM | anim dictionaries `.ycd` in `stream/`, played with `RequestAnimDict`+`TaskPlayAnim`; vehicle doors/bones, ptfx assets (`.ypt`), via natives (door natives and ptfx native names U) | Yes, `stream/` is server-streamed | Reuse existing dict/clip names = easy; authoring new ycd needs CodeWalker/Sollumz (no-licence / GPL) | GO as "pick from existing dictionaries + ptfx presets"; NO-GO for authoring new ycd (V docs.fivem.net TASK_PLAY_ANIM_ADVANCED; wiki.gtaconnected requestAnims; rest U) |
| Source / GMod | QC `$sequence`, SMD/DMX, studiomdl; PCF particles (V developer.valvesoftware.com) | Workshop `.gma` | Medium; compile needs Windows + game | LATER |
| Palworld / ARK (Unreal) | AnimSequence/Montage/Niagara cooked into pak; pak mods usually need each client to install; UE4SS mods not usable on dedicated servers (V indifferentbroccoli wiki, nexusmods) | Palworld no; ASA via CurseForge ID | Low (cook toolchain) | NO-GO |
| Unturned (Unity) | AnimationClips in master bundle via MasterBundleTool; gun clips Equip/Reload/Hammer/etc. (V docs.smartlydressedgames.com via search) | Workshop auto-download | Medium, needs Unity editor | LATER |

## 4. AI feasibility

| Reliable (Claude) | Not reliable |
|---|---|
| Parametric gaits (walk/run: phase, stride, bob, swing amplitudes per archetype), as already done by creature templates | Mocap-quality human motion, nuanced acting, retargeted dance |
| Mechanical motion: hinges, slides, recoil kicks, slide/bolt cycles, wheel spin, with eased keyframes | Free-form quadruped/creature gaits without a template |
| State machines and trigger wiring (events to sound/particle/light) | Frame-accurate timing by ear (needs human nudge against the waveform) |
| Particle presets by parameters (count, speed, spread, colour ramp, lifetime) | Photoreal fire/water |

Cheapest approach: preset library (kind `motion`/`effect`) + generators with a few typed knobs + AI picks/parameterises/composes + human fixes in the studio timeline. Always validate against caps and show a simulated preview before export (U, consistent with how designer/ and creature/ already work).

## 5. Recommended architecture

**Motion core (game-neutral, pure TS, Zod, like RigSpec/designer):** `MotionSpec v1 { clips[], machines[], rig?, caps }`.
- Track kinds: `transform` (target node, channel pos/rot/scale, keys with ease), `particle` (preset ref + params + emitter node + start/duration), `sound-cue` (sound id from Sound Studio, tick, gain/pitch), `light-material` (emissive/colour/opacity/texture-frame), `event` (named marker, state transition).
- Time in integer ticks at 20 Hz canonical, fractional allowed; exporters resample (Minecraft 1 tick, Hytale fps, Source/Unity per spec).
- Node targets are named rig nodes (`bone`, `socket`, `hinge{axis,limits}`, `wheel{axle}`), so vehicle rigs, gun parts and creature bones are one concept. Attach = `parent` change event (character into seat socket).
- State machine: states (clip, loop mode), transitions (event/guard/min-time), on-enter actions. Triggers come from the ability graph via a `play_effect` / `trigger_motion` action.
- Caps: duration, tracks, keys, particles, live entities, machine states (reuse designer BUDGET semantics).

**Simulator contract:** `sample(spec, state, t) -> Pose + FiredEvents[]` pure and deterministic; `Clock` API (play/pause/seek/scrub, tick rate) exposed by the Model Studio viewport (layers 1-2); three.js adapter maps Pose to Mixer/object transforms; physics (Rapier) only for vehicle dynamics preview, never part of exported truth.

**Exporter contract per game:** `capabilities(game) -> {trackKinds, maxEntities, tickRate, delivery}`; `lower(spec, caps) -> {artifacts, warnings, dropped[]}` so unsupported tracks degrade with an explicit report. Minecraft: transform tracks lower to display-entity interpolation segments, sound/particle cues to scheduler tasks (plugin, within budget), item states to `items/*.json`; creature clips lower to BetterModel `.bbmodel` animation (RigSpec becomes a subset). FiveM adapter later: clip refs to existing dict/name, ptfx refs, door natives.

**Catalog:** presets with kind `motion` / `effect`, per-game support flags, provenance, licence class; AI composes from presets first.

**Ties:** Texture Studio: `light-material` texture-frame track drives `.mcmeta` animated textures and decal swaps; onion-skin already planned. Sound Studio: `sound-cue` references library sound ids; timeline shows waveform with markers snapping to ticks. Model Studio layers 1-2 provide clock and timeline UI; Motion core is the data model both edit.

**Cheapest first slice (end to end):** one item with a gun-state FSM (idle/fire/reload) plus a door prop hinge, in Minecraft display entities + item_model states: spec -> sampler -> three.js preview with scrubber and event log -> exporter emitting plugin-driven display-entity tween + sound cue + `spawn_particles` within existing budgets -> verify on a real 1.21.x and 26.x server. Defer vehicles, BetterModel unification, and non-Minecraft adapters until the core schema survives this slice.
# S: Free motion / effects assets staged for Cyrus (2026-10-10)

Staged under `/tank/cyrus-library-staging/motion/` (183 MB, no git, no root-disk use). Catalog: `motion/catalog-motion.jsonl` (1,972 rows, sha256 ids, deduped). Ledger: `motion/LICENCE-LEDGER-motion.csv` (50 rows). Rows with `ref:true` point at files already staged by the 3D ingest (not moved, not touched). Scripts: `motion/build_catalog.py`, `ogadl.py`, `glbscan.py`. OGA fetched at its 10 s crawl-delay with an identifying UA, one request at a time; KayKit via the normal itch free-download button flow.

## Per source: licence, counts, decision

| Source / pack | Licence (read on page) | Counts | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| KayKit Character Animations 1.1 (itch/kaylousberg.com) | CC0, License.txt quoted: "free to use in personal, educational and commercial projects" | 14 animated glb (Rig_Medium/Large), 173 clips (144 unique names), clip durations recorded | ACCEPT cc0 (free upload only; paid Source tier not used) |
| Quaternius Universal Animation Library 1+2 (already staged) | CC0 | 4 glb, 172 clip rows (86 unique; std + root-motion) | ACCEPT cc0, ref |
| 3D-ingest animated models (Quaternius, Kenney, KayKit, Khronos, Poly Haven) | CC0, plus 12 Khronos CC-BY 4.0 | 390 glb contain animation; 5,786 embedded clips (heavy duplication, same clip set per character) | ACCEPT per tier, ref |
| OpenGameArt effects (28 pages) | CC0 per asset page; 3 pages CC-BY | 127 sheets/atlases, 37 frame-sequence folders (822 frames), 238 loose sprite frames | ACCEPT; CC-BY in separate tier |
| OGA Quaternius creature FBX (animals, farm, monsters, fish, robot, animated guns) | CC0 | 30 FBX, 94 clip stacks (guns: Fire/Reload/Slide x5 weapons) | ACCEPT cc0; needs FBX to glTF conversion (no converter on this box) |
| RPicster Godot particle/VFX textures (GitHub) | CC0, LICENSE file + README quoted | 42 particle/lensflare/light textures (64/256/1024) | ACCEPT cc0 |
| Kenney Particle Pack, Smoke Particles, Splat Pack, Light Masks (already staged) | CC0 | 761 PNG (black + transparent variants of the same art) | ACCEPT cc0, ref |
| OGA Low Poly Doors Asset | CC0 | 1 gltf + 22 fbx, 0 clips (static) | Kept, not in catalog |
| Mixamo | free, no redistribution as library | none | REJECT |
| CMU mocap, Tiddybub/2d-assets, Indosaram/pixel-vfx-local, slippylabs/particle-forge | redistribution limits, or no usable licence file | none | REJECT |
| Blender Studio vault | CC-BY, membership needed | none | SKIP |
| Poly Haven | CC0 but nothing motion-related | none | N/A |
| itch.io CC0 VFX packs (Aim Studios, Stealthix, TornadoGames, GoVFX) | claimed CC0 in search snippets, not verified on page | none | DEFERRED (owner hand-pick) |

Rejected on page: OGA collection pages (Graphic FX, 2D::Animation/Effect, Effect&Shader, 05 Pixel Art) have no files of their own. Quaternius FBX copies of packs already staged as glb were downloaded then deleted as duplicates.

## Totals by kind and tier

| Kind | CC0 | CC-BY | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| animation-clip | 345 rows (230 unique names) | 0 | KayKit 173 + UAL 172 |
| animated-model | 408 (364 ref glb, 14 KayKit glb, 30 FBX) | 12 (Khronos, ref) | 390 glb animated, validated by parsing |
| flipbook | 118 sheets + 37 sequences (822 frames) + 238 sprite frames | 9 sheets | grid size only known from filenames (some 512 px cells in 4096 atlases); the rest need a grid-detect pass |
| particle-texture | 805 (42 RPicster, 2 OGA, 761 Kenney ref) | 0 | |
| effect-preset | 0 | 0 | none exist with a clean licence |

CC-BY attribution (recorded in catalog): "Muzzle Flash" by Aech (CC-BY 3.0); "AlotofImpacts" by JoesAlotofthings (CC-BY 4.0); "Explosion effects and more" by Soluna Software (dual CC-BY 3.0 / CC0, author says no credit needed); Khronos models per the 3D catalog.

Checks: all new glb parsed (JSON chunk, BIN bounds); all PNG/GIF opened with PIL; 0 odd files, nothing quarantined. Older 3D-ingest "Animated*" Quaternius packs (dinosaurs, guns, tanks, fish, zombie, alien, etc.) are static glb with zero animations, so only the OGA FBX copies above carry those clips.

## Gaps against the owner's list

| Effect | Free coverage |
|---|---|
| Explosion | Good as 2D flipbooks (Sinestesia 512 px atlases, more-explosions, Soluna); no 3D or volumetric |
| Fire | Good (439-frame fire/spell sets, animated fire, flame sheets) |
| Smoke | Good (Smoke Aura 91 frames, Kenney smoke, smoke sheet) |
| Muzzle flash / impacts | Good (about 270 sprites, 16 toon, hit animation) |
| Water splash / flow | Weak: one 3-frame splash and rain drops. Water flow has nothing; needs a shader plus normal map (ambientCG is staged) |
| Gun cocking | Covered by Quaternius animated guns (Reload, Slide, Fire for pistol/revolver/rifle/shotgun/P90) and UAL Pistol_Reload; needs FBX conversion |
| Creature walk/attack | Strong (cute monsters, animals, dragon/bat/slime, 397+ clip names) |
| Door / mechanism | No animation. UAL has Chest_Open/Interact for the character side only. Hinge door tracks must be authored; static door geometry is on disk |
| Car door | Nothing |

Verdict: free assets cover textures and flipbooks for fire, smoke, explosion and muzzle, plus character and creature clips. Effect presets (parameter JSON), water, doors, mechanisms and vehicle doors must be authored by us, using these flipbooks as the texture inputs.

## Owner decisions

1. CC-BY tier: accept the 9 CC-BY sheets (attribution page needed) or drop them. The Soluna pack can be treated as CC0 if you accept the dual-listing.
2. KayKit/Quaternius ask people not to resell unmodified copies. It is a courtesy request, not a licence term, but a bulk library redistribution should be modified or curated.
3. FBX to glTF: approve installing a converter (or a node FBXLoader script) in an isolated place so the 30 creature and gun FBX files become glb.
4. MIT or Apache preset repos (such as tsparticles) were not staged because only CC0/CC-BY is allowed; say if permissive licences are acceptable for effect presets.
5. itch.io CC0 VFX packs: hand-pick a few if you want more fire and explosion variety.

# Cyrus full plan: separation, bridge, portals, infra, one-session updates (2026-10-11)
Companion to CYRUS-TRACKER.md (state) and MASTER-PLAN.md (engine). Estimates are my judgement, not measurements.

## 0. Target architecture (what "done" looks like)
```
 cyrus.my (landing, Cloudflare)      app.cyrus.my  (Cyrus customer app)      admin.cyrus.my (Cyrus admin)
                          \               |                    /
                           +---- Cyrus services: API (api.cyrus.my) + workers + own DB + object storage/CDN + build service
                                          |  ^
                    Cyrus -> Nxeon:       |  |   Nxeon -> Cyrus:
                    Nxeon Platform API    |  |   Cyrus API v1 + signed webhooks
                    (identity, wallet,    v  |   (projects, builds, mods, entitlements)
                     servers, files)   nxeon.cloud (portal, billing, game servers, admin)
```
Principles: (1) Nxeon = identity + money + game-server hosting; Cyrus = everything about mods. (2) One account, one wallet, one Stripe. (3) The browser talks straight to the service that owns the feature; no relaying. (4) Every cross-app call is a versioned, tested contract. (5) Nothing in Nxeon breaks at any step: each phase is flag-gated and reversible.

## 1. Decisions to lock first (my recommendation in bold)
1. Repo shape: **one monorepo, several deployables** (`apps/nxeon`, `apps/cyrus`, `apps/cyrus-admin`, `apps/cyrus-site`, `packages/*` shared). One Claude session edits one repo and ships only what changed. Separate repos would make "one update applies everywhere" a cross-repo chore.
2. Payment: **Nxeon wallet/Stripe is the only money system** (already the coded default). Cyrus sells nothing itself; it asks Nxeon to charge.
3. Identity: **Nxeon is the identity provider**; cyrus.my accounts are lazily provisioned Nxeon accounts. "Sign in with Cyrus" on Nxeon is a button that lands on the same account.
4. Server access: **per-server, scoped grants** (section 3.3), never SSH credentials.
5. Hosting for Cyrus services: own VPS/dedicated pair (app + build/worker) behind Cloudflare; **separate Postgres** from Nxeon. Region chosen deliberately (primary is Singapore, node-2 Germany).
6. Admin: **Cyrus has its own admin; Nxeon admin shows a read-only Cyrus summary + deep link**; staff identity and roles come from Nxeon rbac.
7. Terms: separate Cyrus ToS/Privacy (with the library licence grant), reviewed by a lawyer before public launch.

## 2. Phases (order matters; each ends in something shippable)
**P0 Today, 1-2 h owner time: decisions + reviews.** Lock section 1; review the landing page when ready; skim v2/v3/v4/v5 mockups (they gate UI polish, not the backbone).
**P1 Front door (today).** Landing page review, then publish it as the cyrus.my static site (swap into /var/www/cyrus.my). Dual-host shell + SSO + purchase->credit (agent r36 running). Cert watcher finishes TLS when Cloudflare activates the zone.
**P2 Cloudflare for Nxeon (today/tomorrow, needs a zone token).** Restore real client IP (CF-Connecting-IP) in nginx + app first; proxy one hostname, then portal/site; keep game, mail and non-HTTP records grey; cache static only; websocket keepalive; Full (strict); measure US load time before/after.
**P3 Extract the Cyrus app (1-2 days of agent work).** Monorepo scaffold; `apps/cyrus` as its own Next app (own layout, own session cookie, own routes: dashboard, studios, library, mods, plans); move `components/cyrus`, `lib/cyrus`, `app/**/cyrus*` into packages/app; the 5 remaining baseline imports and the 185 app/component imports of Nxeon code are replaced by the host seam or shared packages (`packages/ui` for primitives, `packages/auth-client`, `packages/nxeon-client`, `packages/cyrus-client`); the Nxeon portal's Cyrus tab becomes thin (list, status, deep links, embed-free). Both still deploy from one place at first.
**P4 Bridge hardening (1-2 days, parallel with P3 where files differ).** Section 3 in full: Nxeon Platform API for servers/files with scoped grants, entitlement sync, webhooks live in the product, notifications, support context, server-aware Cyrus UX.
**P5 Data split (half a day + careful cutover).** Cyrus tables to their own database (28 tables, no FKs, user ids are plain strings; Nxeon-table access already gone via `cyrusDb`); dual-write or dump/restore with a short write freeze; rollback = repoint. Own backups from day one.
**P6 Portals (2-3 days, parallel agents).** Section 4 (customer) and section 5 (admin).
**P7 Infra move (1 day + soak).** New servers, Cloudflare in front, R2/CDN for packs and library, build service wiring, staging env, monitoring, backups, status page, deploy script with health-checked cutover and rollback (`promote-cyrus.sh`, same safety rules as promote-production.sh).
**P8 Launch gate (owner-gated).** Real-client test day, paid eval baseline + fix loop, API key replaces subscription login, legal, migrations/runbook (docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md + CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md), then flag order with the launch-pair guard.
Realistic today: P0, P1, start P2 (needs token), kick off P3 scaffolding. P3-P7 are multi-day even with parallel agents; the build lock on node-2 and your usage are the limits, not ideas.

## 3. The bridge, in detail
### 3.1 Identity and account lifecycle
Stable subject id (Nxeon user id) everywhere; never match on email. Sign in with Nxeon on cyrus.my (OIDC-style redirect, state/nonce, signed assertion, own session cookie); "Sign in with Cyrus" on Nxeon goes to the same account. First visit provisions the Cyrus profile silently (no second signup). Gaps to cover: verified email required; MFA lives at Nxeon; per-host sessions + back-channel logout; account suspend/ban propagation both ways (Cyrus-only abuse flags a user at Nxeon); deletion + data export cascade (GDPR) across both; Cyrus ToS acceptance recorded per user with version; admin view-as across hosts without leaking; account merge when someone already has two identities.
### 3.2 Money, plans, tokens
Plans (Katara, Saka, Yakko) and token packs are products in Nxeon billing; entitlement is Nxeon's, mirrored into Cyrus by webhook + short-TTL cache, **fail closed** when unknown. Purchases started on either site go through Nxeon checkout; credit to Cyrus tokens is idempotent (outbox, retries, daily reconciliation, honest pending/failed states); refunds and chargebacks reverse credits; invoices/VAT stay in Nxeon. Gaps: Creator Partner Program attribution for Cyrus plans (50% first / 10% recurring exists at Nxeon: decide if it applies); promo codes; free-tier grants and abuse limits; spend caps per user and global (AI cost vs revenue dashboard); tax/VAT decision still open.
### 3.3 Connecting servers ("install straight onto my servers")
Connect = a consent screen at Nxeon listing exactly what Cyrus may do, per server the user ticks. Scopes: `servers.read` (id, name, game, version/loader, status, RAM/CPU, player count), `inventory.read` (installed plugins/mods with versions: feeds the conflict engine before every build/install), `files.write.mods` (only mods/plugins/config/datapack/resource-pack paths, with hash preconditions), `server.reload` / `server.restart` (budgeted), `logs.read.tail` (for Server Doctor, health, post-install checks), `pack.set` (resource-pack URL + hash). Cyrus keeps the delivery orchestrator (journal, rollback); Nxeon exposes safe primitives and audits every call. Revocable any time; every call tied to user + server + grant; rate limited; idempotent. Webhooks Nxeon -> Cyrus: `server.version_changed` (mark mods outdated), `server.deleted`, `server.restarted`, `grant.revoked`. Users without Nxeon servers: download jar, "Try it" throwaway server, install guide. Pull to improve results: target version from the server, RAM-aware warnings (worldgen, creatures), existing-plugin conflicts, "Create a mod for this server" button on every Nxeon server page that prefills Cyrus.
### 3.4 Cross-product experience
Shared header package (account menu, balance, notifications, product switcher); deep links with silent SSO; one notification system (build finished, install result, mod outdated, takedown) with one preference center, email through Nxeon's mail stack from a cyrus.my sender (SPF/DKIM/DMARC for the new domain); support: tickets stay in Nxeon, carry Cyrus context (build id, spec, flight record), support can view-as; unified status page; cross-domain analytics/attribution (Meta/Google conversions, referral cookies) and a cookie-consent banner; SEO: `/mods/cyrus` redirect strategy to cyrus.my.

## 4. Cyrus customer app (app.cyrus.my): what it needs
Dashboard (projects, recent builds, mods, plan + tokens, connected servers, library contributions, activity); project page (revisions, builds with Test Flight status, install/rollback, configs, studios: texture, sound, model, motion, designers, config); new-mod flow with game/version/server pickers and cost shown first; library browser; mod pages (public, pass-rate badges, ratings); account (profile, connected Nxeon account + servers + grants, personal Cyrus API keys, notification prefs, data export/delete); plans/tokens (buy via Nxeon); onboarding tour and templates gallery; docs/help; changelog (customer-facing only); teams/shared projects (later, a real gap); referral/creator pages.
## 5. Admin portal (admin.cyrus.my, staff via Nxeon roles)
Overview (queue depth, build success rate, spend vs revenue, errors); builds (search, logs, rerun, kill, cost); users (lookup, plan/tokens adjust with audit, view-as, ban/suspend, GDPR tools); library moderation (hold queue, takedown/DMCA log, near-duplicate tools, trademark/real-weapon lists); flags and kill switches (launch-pair guard, AI gateway kill, global build pause, per-feature off); evals and pass-rates (run, compare, publish); capacity (build VM, node-2 flights, meshgen jobs, storage); cost governance (per-model spend, per-user caps, alerts); audit log; announcements; reconciliation view (Nxeon wallet vs Cyrus tokens, webhook failures, replay). Nxeon admin gets a read-only Cyrus card + deep link.

## 6. Cloudflare and infrastructure
cyrus.my zone (pending): apex + www (landing static), app, api, admin, cdn/packs (R2) subdomains; WAF + rate limits, Turnstile on sign-up and "Create Mod", bot protection; Full (strict) with origin certs; static cache rules; pack and library delivery from R2/CDN with signed URLs (sound library only when cleared). Nxeon zones per P2 (client IP first, game and mail records stay grey). Own Postgres + PgBouncer, nightly encrypted backups off-box, second copy of the proprietary SFX library (tank is one disk with no redundancy). Staging environment; observability (logs, metrics, uptime, error tracking, per-build cost telemetry); status page; secrets in one place; **the build service must move from subscription login to an API key before any public launch** with hard spend caps; build-queue fairness and capacity plan beyond the single build VM.

## 7. One Claude session updates everything
Monorepo layout above. `scripts/ship <target|all>` detects what changed (apps and packages graph), runs tests + the seam ratchet + OpenAPI contract tests, builds on node-2 (never in the live tree), deploys through health-checked promote scripts with auto-rollback: nxeon (existing promote-production.sh), cyrus app + api + worker (`promote-cyrus.sh`), landing (rsync to /var/www/cyrus.my or Cloudflare Pages), admin. Shared packages guarantee "same behaviour" across nxeon.cloud, cyrus.my and the Nxeon tab; API contracts are versioned (v1 stays until v2 proven; expand/contract DB migrations; N and N-1 compatible) so deploy order never breaks anything; flags allow dark launches and instant rollback. Rule kept: never edit or build in /opt/nxeon; worktrees + devhost; deploy only through the promote scripts.

## 8. Gaps and improvements to remember
Teams/shared projects; public developer API + personal API keys with docs.cyrus.my; mod marketplace/NxLabs listings, ratings, reports, and the parked Mojang EULA/marketplace question; moderation SLAs; DMCA/takedown process and counter-notice; per-user AI spend caps; data residency/GDPR export-delete; accessibility audit; email deliverability for cyrus.my; Discord/community; localisation (later); webhooks retry dashboards; load test before launch; disaster-recovery drill; customer support macros; pricing page truthfulness (no invented prices or stats); .my domain registrant/legal pages.

## 9. Today (suggested order)
1. You: confirm section 1 decisions (10 min). 2. Me: finish landing review -> publish to cyrus.my. 3. # Cyrus Master Plan: the ultimate game-mod creation studio (Minecraft first)

Date: 2026-10-10. Owner direction: build the ultimate mod creation studio; launch is months away; other concerns later. Sources: the four owner documents (Master Update Plan, Texture & Sound plan, Minecraft Feature Roadmap, multi-game prompt), research files E, G, A, A2, B, C, D, F, and the red-team review GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md, all in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/`. Research claims are labelled VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED in those files; this plan inherits their labels and adds none of its own. Sizes are S/M/L effort.

## 1. What we are building
A real game-mod **engine**, not a prompt box. The source of truth is a typed, versioned **mod project**; the AI is the author and editor inside it; deterministic generators, validators and a real-server test harness turn the project into artifacts; studios and designers edit the same project; mods compose into Mod Packs; users can bring their own mods. Minecraft is adapter #1 on a game-agnostic core.

**Principles**
1. Engine first: every feature must be typed, validated, testable, editable and composable. A prompt wrapper is not a feature.
2. Evidence over claims: no status ("built", "tested", "supported") that did not actually run. Compile, scan, boot test and functional test are separate checks.
3. Foundation for other games: shared core behind interfaces; per-game adapters (Section 4.10).
4. Honest about limits: the router tells users what a vanilla client can and cannot do.
5. Dependencies decide order, not enthusiasm (the review found five dependency inversions in the first schedule; this plan fixes them).

## 2. Decisions already made by the owner
- Plan tiers: Free and Katara get no studios; **Saka gets Sound Studio + Sound Library; the top plan (`all`, includes Yakko) gets everything** including Texture Studio + Texture Library. Tiers are cumulative.
- **Automatic asset generation follows the user's plan and access** (same gate whether Cyrus, the studio or a library creates the asset).
- **Mod Packs are not gated by plan. Importing your own mod to work on it is not gated by plan.**
- Asset libraries and studios are top priorities; the owner's 514-file sound library is the Sound Library seed.
- Everything in scope, ambitious timeline; launch is months away. Research ran as limited Sonnet agents; no parallel agent sprawl.
- Parked by the owner ("later"): Mojang EULA / marketplace question, other-platform AI policies (Modrinth etc.), licence review of dependencies. Not worked in this plan.

**Defaults I set (change any of them):**
- Gate semantics: gates apply to **creating or editing** assets. Installing, keeping, rebuilding unchanged and exporting existing project assets is never gated. The router downgrades (no custom asset) instead of erroring, and gating fails closed when token state is unknown.
- Banshee on 1.21.x = custom skin + full sound set on a vanilla-model mob; **animated custom-model creatures are 26.x first** (BetterModel v3 needs Java 25).
- Generated mods stay on `plugin.yml` (Paper's `paper-plugin.yml` is still experimental).
- Gameplay Designers, full creature pipeline and worldgen come after the foundation, assets and composition (they are mini-languages each).

## 2b. Built to stand alone later (owner decision, 2026-10-10)
Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.

## 3. Reality check on the facts (from the research)
- Cyrus builds only 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 on JDK 21. Compile is plain `javac --release 21 -proc:none` against a Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files). 4 of 6 explicitly versioned Paper servers on Nxeon already run 26.x, so version support is a top lever. 26.x needs Java 25. **Correction (checked on Paper's Fill API and Maven, 2026-10-10):** stable builds exist only for 26.1.2 (build 74) and 26.2 (build 133); 26.3 has only alpha/beta builds, so the version research was wrong that 26.3 is stable. The 26.x lane starts with **26.2**, then 26.1.2; 26.3 stays preview and unpinned until Paper ships a stable build. The registry now holds the exact pins and server-jar hashes.
- No ModSpec, project/revision store, asset manifest or import flow exist. A "project" is a chain of `ModBuild` rows. `textures/` does item textures only; `sfx.ts` is interface sounds only. The Mods installer treats resource packs as unsupported. `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x (returns 75; 26.1 is 76-84). Plan tiers gate models only; the single gate is `gateBuild` at `create.ts:72`, bypassed when tokens are off.
- `server.properties` holds one resource pack; Paper's `Player#addResourcePack(UUID, ...)` allows several and `setResourcePack` is deprecated.
- A vanilla client with a server-pushed pack plus datapack can show items, weapons, armor, food, display-entity mobs, glyph HUDs, GUIs, enchantments, recipes, advancements, bosses, abilities, commands, sounds, biomes and structures. Client-mod-only: brand-new block types, native entity models, free-form HUD widgets, custom keybinds, custom sky.
- Build service auth: it can run on a subscription login. Before ANY public launch, switch to an API key and re-measure cost (not blocking development now).
- Jars are not reproducible today (`jar --create` without `--date`).

## 4. Engine design
### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.

### 4.11 Data packs (M)
Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.

### R5 Beyond Minecraft Java (own programmes)
Fabric client-mod pipeline (narrow); the other five games as adapters (multi-game prompt, per-game maturity ladder); realistic 3D/PBR asset profile; Bedrock conversion. Each starts only when the previous layers are stable.

## 6. Cross-cutting
- **Testing/eval**: extend the existing harness (28 prompts, 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6) to 100+ prompts per version; golden pack snapshots (canonical JSON + sorted file list + sha1); property tests for merge laws (idempotent, order-stable, no key loss); javap-verified API sheets in CI; contract test of the version registry; mutation corpus for conflicts. Per-version pass rates published only when measured.
- **Quality bar**: Style DNA, rubric metrics, vision-judge calibration, owner gallery sign-off.
- **Pricing**: show an estimate before building; price assets by measured work; no charge if validation fails before delivery; per-feature reserve rows (reconcile `katara/saka/yakko` vs `katara/saka/all` naming); free tier gets no assets and per-device/IP caps.
- **Operations**: treat prompt + sheets + rules + scanner + image as one engine release with canary and auto-rollback on eval regression; per-feature kill switches (asset generation, import, packs); node-2 capacity budget for test servers; prompt-injection hygiene (imported text only as quoted data, no network for the model, path allow-list on diffs).
- **Security**: scanner remains a policy check, not proof; fail closed; import profiles warn honestly; supply-chain pinning (sha256, image digests, lockfiles).
- **Telemetry funnel**: prompt -> spec -> build -> pass -> install -> pack accepted -> player joined -> day-7 retention; gate impressions and upgrade conversion.

## 7. Risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Schedule: sizes in the research sum to roughly 25-35 engineer-weeks for the asset/composition/designer scope | Dependency-ordered phases; real-client and owner waits scheduled; creature/designers/worldgen after the foundation |
| Real-client tests (T) cannot be automated | Name a standing tester; small matrix per asset day |
| BetterModel v3/v2 split and Java 25 | Creatures 26.x first; pinned managed plugin; test before relying on 1.21.1 |
| Paper experimental APIs (paper-plugin.yml, data components) | Generated mods on plugin.yml; isolate experiments in the Nxeon-owned loader; monthly CI |
| Beta builds via floating coordinates | Pin exact stable; nightly check |
| Import hardness (dependencies, scanner bans reflection/network that legitimate plugins use) | Allowlist + attested profile; source-only first |
| Scanner false sense of safety | Honest labels; no "safe" claim for imports |
| Cost blowout from asset critique loops | Cap rounds, cache by spec hash, per-build cost cap |
| Public pass-rate claims | Publish only measured numbers per version |
| Build service auth (subscription login) | API key + re-measured pricing before ANY public launch |

## 8. Owner actions to line up
VM 88001 update and image rebuild (JDK 25 beside 21) and the hardened scan check; DB migration deploy approval (project/revision tables); object storage + domain for packs; a standing person with Minecraft for (T) days (and later Fabric); confirm or change the defaults in Section 2; weekly-usage allowance for the build weeks; API-key switch before public launch.

## 9. Open questions
1. Is the banshee-on-1.21.x default (skin + sounds) acceptable, with animated creatures on 26.x first?
2. Confirm the gate semantics default (create/edit gated; install/keep/export never).
3. Who is the standing tester and on which days?
4. Do you want Server Doctor (scan any customer server for conflicts) as an early acquisition feature?
5. Which object storage and domain for packs?

# Valheim in Cyrus: readiness checklist (2026-10-08)

Status: **`soon`** (not flipped; going `live` is the owner's call). Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-valheim`.

## What is done
- [x] `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.ts`: verified `GameSupport` (versions 1.0.x current / 0.221.x legacy / older unsupported, install side + plain-language reasons, breakage risks, outdated signals, 12 universal categories, sources, unknowns) and `VALHEIM_TARGET` (game line 1.0, network 40, BepInExPack 5.4.2351, Jötunn 2.30.2).
- [x] `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts`: Valheim 1.0 knowledge pack (`GameSupport.knowledge`): ~28 verified API facts + 11 failure rules with regex detectors; `apiLinesFor()` for selective retrieval.
- [x] Generator `lib/cyrus/engine/games/valheim.ts` upgraded for 1.0 (see the report for the fixed bugs), version-aware (`cyrus.json`, startup version check), Thunderstore-correct manifest, Jötunn version enforcement for content mods, AI disclosure, runnable xUnit project for Yakko.
- [x] Validator `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.validate.ts` + tests `test/cyrus-game-valheim.test.ts`.
- [x] Compile harness `tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/` (node-2): every template compiled against the real 1.0.16 dedicated-server assemblies + generated tests run.

## Before Valheim can go live
### Must have
1. **Real AI generation path.** Today non-Minecraft games stream *template* code (`lib/cyrus/engine`), not model output. A real Valheim build needs the build service to accept `game: "valheim"`: a C# worker on the build VM with the .NET 8 SDK, the knowledge pack in the prompt (`apiLinesFor` on the plan), the validator as the safety scan, and `dotnet build` against the game assemblies as the compile step. (Build-VM changes are owner-only.)
2. **Game assemblies on the build host, never redistributed.** The harness downloads the free dedicated server's `Managed/*.dll` from Steam (app 896660, anonymous, public) at build time into a node-2 cache. The owner should confirm this is acceptable for a commercial build pipeline (it is how the repo's NxeonDevAdmin plugin is already built). Nothing proprietary is committed.
3. **Load test in a real server.** A throwaway Valheim dedicated server (Docker `lloesche/valheim-server` with `BEPINEX=true`, already used by Nxeon) on node-2 or a sandbox VM: install the DLL + Jötunn, start, grep `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` for `<Name> v1.0.0 loaded`, no Harmony errors, and for content mods that ZNetScene registered the prefab. Then a headless client check is not possible; client-side mods (HUD, music, grading) need one manual PC test per archetype.
4. **End-to-end customer test on a real Nxeon Valheim server**: generate → validate → install via the Mods tab (`lib/mods/installers/valheim.ts`, plugin folder `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Ns>-<Name>`) → restart → join with r2modman carrying the same mod → verify the feature in game → disable → confirm the removal warning was shown. Owner/test account only.
5. **Client-install guidance in the UI** (lifecycle/studio agents): show `cyrus.json.install.note` on the install card; for `side: both`, offer a download of the mod zip and an r2modman profile code for players; warn "console players will not be able to join" when the server has crossplay on.
6. **icon.png (256x256)** for the Thunderstore zip: the generator does not create one; the listing flow must add the creator's icon or the compact Cyrus badge.

### Should have
7. **Version table maintenance.** After every Valheim patch: `CYRUS_VH_REFRESH=1 devhost run --lock -- bash tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/run.sh`; if green, bump `VALHEIM_TARGET.game/verifiedBuild` and (when released) `bepinexPack`/`jotunn`; if red, add a failure rule and fix the generator. Cadence seen: major engine upgrades 2024-04 (Unity 2022), 2025-08 (Unity 6, 0.221.3), 2026-09 (1.0); small patches every 1 to 3 weeks after 1.0.
8. **Outdated watcher** (lifecycle agent): poll Thunderstore for BepInExPack_Valheim / Jötunn and Steam for app 896660 build changes; mark installed Cyrus mods "may need an update" when the game line moves, and tell creators (`outdatedSignals`).
9. **Golden examples** (research item 3): 3 to 5 hand-checked Valheim mods, compiled + load-tested, used as few-shot context and regression tests.
10. **Eval suite** (designed, not run, cost rule): 30 prompts across the 12 categories + 10 adversarial (network, file deletion, admin list, cheats) scored on validator pass, compile pass, load pass.

### Nice to have
11. Asset pipeline for custom models/textures (Unity AssetBundles built with the matching Unity 6 editor; Unity licence terms not checked yet; see research RENDERS-AND-TEXTURES.md).
12. ServerSync-style config locking so server admins' config wins over clients (Jötunn `AdminOnly` config entries are the lighter option).

## Owner decisions
- Accept downloading the public dedicated-server DLLs at build time for compile checks (never shipped)?
- AI disclosure text: generated mods say "created with the assistance of generative AI (Nxeon Cyrus)" in README/csproj, as Thunderstore requires. OK to name only Cyrus and its model names?
- Should Cyrus allow publishing Valheim mods to Thunderstore at all? Its rules reject "untested or non-functional AI-generated mods"; recommend: only after the load test (step 3) passes, and never auto-publish.
- Content mods force Jötunn (for version enforcement). Accept the extra dependency for players?

# Cyrus · Terraria: readiness checklist + how Terraria modding works

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-terraria` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-game-terraria`). Written 2026-10-08.
Status in `lib/cyrus/games.ts`: **not flipped to live** (owner's call).

## Verdict first: two products on two game versions

| | TShock server plugin | tModLoader content mod |
|---|---|---|
| Game version | **Terraria 1.4.5.8** | **Terraria 1.4.4.9** |
| Loader | TShock 6.2.1 (TerrariaServerAPI 2.1, .NET 9) | tModLoader v2026.08.3.0 stable (.NET 8) |
| Players install | nothing | tModLoader (free Steam app, needs Terraria); the server sends the mod on join |
| What it can do | commands, permissions, rewards, events, vanilla items/enemies/bosses/buffs | anything new: items, enemies, bosses, mounts, biomes/world gen, UI, music, screen effects |
| **Runs on a Nxeon Terraria server today** | **Yes.** New servers run `ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock:6.2.1`; plugins go in `/opt/terraria-plugins` and the existing installer restarts and confirms TShock's "Plugin X vY initiated." line (rolls back otherwise). | **No.** Nxeon never installs tModLoader. A tModLoader mod built by Cyrus can be downloaded and used on the player's own tModLoader server, nowhere on Nxeon yet. |

tModLoader has not moved to 1.4.5 (a contributor-only `1.4.5-dev` beta exists; "many months" per
tModLoader issue #5070), so a tModLoader server and a 1.4.5 TShock server cannot share players. They are two products.
Cyrus picks the flavour per request, records it in `cyrus.mod.json` (`flavor`, `target`, `side`, `playersInstall`),
and the validator refuses any file that mixes TShock and tModLoader code. The Nxeon installer already refuses
non-TShock Terraria mods (`lib/mod-install-support.ts`).

## What was verified for real (2026-10-08)

- Every API the generator emits compiles: **78/78** generated mods (26 prompts x Katara/Saka/Yakko) via
  `scripts/cyrus/terraria-compile-check.sh` on node-2. TShock plugins compile with .NET 9 SDK + the public TShock
  6.2.1 NuGet package to a `.dll`; tModLoader mods compile with .NET 8 SDK + the public tModLoader v2026.08.3.0 release
  and are packaged to a real `.tmod` by tModLoader's own `-build`. No game files were needed or used.
- Static validator + 100+ pure unit tests (`test/cyrus-game-terraria.test.ts`).
- NOT verified: that the mods load and behave in a running game/server (no load-test yet), how placeholder art looks,
  balance.

## Readiness checklist (what is left before Terraria can go live)

### Must have (TShock plugins, the part that can run on Nxeon)
1. **Compile step in the Cyrus pipeline.** Today the compile runs only in the dev harness. The build service
   (`services/modbuilder/`, owned elsewhere) needs a Terraria job: write files, `dotnet build -c Release` with the TShock
   package from a local NuGet cache, return `<Name>.dll` only (not the TShock dlls copied next to it), sandboxed (no
   network after restore, CPU/memory/time caps). The commands are in the harness script.
2. **Validator gate.** Call `validateTerraria(files)` before showing a build; block on `severity: "block"`.

# Project Zomboid in Cyrus: readiness checklist and explainer (2026-10-08)

Status: **not live** (`soon`). Flipping it to live is the owner's decision. Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-zomboid`.

## What is done

- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.ts`: verified GameSupport (versions 42.21 → 41.78, install side `both`, plain-language install text, 17 dangerous-API rules, breakage risks with guards, outdated signals, categories, sources, unknowns) plus a `knowledge` pack (14 API-sheet lines, 12 Build 41→42 failure rules with regex detectors).
- `lib/cyrus/engine/games/zomboid.ts`: the template generator rewritten for Build 42.15+ and the 42.13 multiplayer rules (server-authoritative effects, shared timed actions, JSON translations, `ItemType`/registry ids, own script module, per-mod Lua folders, guarded fire, no map files). API check: `API-CHECK.md`.
- `lib/cyrus/games/zomboid.validate.ts`: static validator (layout, mod.info, Lua 5.1 structure lint written in TypeScript, dangerous APIs, failure rules, MP rules, script braces, JSON translations).
- `test/cyrus-game-zomboid.test.ts`: every category × model × six prompts must pass the validator with zero blocking issues, plus negative tests.

## What is left before it can go live

1. **Real-model generation path.** Today Zomboid output comes from the deterministic template, not from the AI build service (which only builds Minecraft). The live product needs the build service to: take the GameSupport `knowledge` pack as context, generate, run `validateZomboidMod`, feed blocking issues back for repair, and only then show the mod. Owner decision: when to wire it, and whether Zomboid gets its own service endpoint.
2. **Load test in a sandbox (not run).** Needs nothing proprietary in git, but it needs compute:
   - Project Zomboid dedicated server, downloaded by SteamCMD anonymously (app **380870**) inside a throwaway container, the same way Nxeon's own Zomboid image installs it. Nothing is redistributed: Valve's tool fetches it into the sandbox.
   - Steps: copy the mod into `<cachedir>/mods/<ModId>/`, set `Mods=<ModId>` in `Server/servertest.ini`, boot with a fresh world, wait for "SERVER STARTED", run a few game minutes, then grep `console.txt` / `Logs/*DebugLog-server.txt` for `ERROR`, `STACK TRACE`, `attempted index`, `Object tried to call nil` mentioning the mod's files. Exit code + log excerpt = the verdict.
   - Lua unit tests: run the generated busted spec with a free Lua 5.1 (`lua5.1` + `busted`, or the open-source `wasmoon`/`fengari` npm packages). Not installed anywhere today; adding them is a dependency or system-package decision for the owner.
   - Limits: a headless server never runs `lua/client` code, so HUDs, context menus and keybinds still need a human (or a scripted client, which is not available).
   - Resources: about 4 to 6 GB RAM and 2 vCPU per test run (Build 42 is heavy; Nxeon sells 6 GB as the smallest Zomboid plan). Must run on a sandbox VM, never on the build VM or a customer VM.
3. **End-to-end test on a real Nxeon 42.21 server.** Confirm: a mod in the cache folder `mods/` loads on the dedicated server with only `Mods=`; the `Mods=`/`WorkshopItems=` format the installer writes (official 42.15 guide: plain MOD_IDs; community sources disagree on a backslash); clients get kicked or warned when files differ; a Workshop-published copy downloads for players on join.
4. **Distribution to players.** Every player needs the same files. The only automatic path is the Steam Workshop, which needs the **creator's own Steam account** (and game licence) to upload; Nxeon cannot upload on a customer's behalf. Owner decision: (a) guide creators to upload via the in-game uploader with a Cyrus-generated `workshop.txt` + preview, or (b) offer "private server pack" downloads that players install by hand. Until then, multiplayer Cyrus mods are only practical for small groups.
5. **Install flow guard.** Nxeon offers PZ variants `b42` (default, stable public branch = 42.21 today) and `b41` (Legacy). Cyrus mods must only install on `b42` servers (lifecycle agent).
6. **Version table maintenance.** On every stable build: read the Steam news feed (app 108600) for "Modding Changelog"/"Migration Guide" posts, re-run the API check against the new JavaDocs, bump `PZ_TARGET.testedOn`, update `versions`, add failure rules. The "Build 42 Support Update" (rest of 2026) promises more modding changes and an official modding guide.
7. **Assets.** Items/vehicles reference icons, models and textures that are not generated; sounds reference `.ogg` clips. `ASSETS.md` lists them. The render/texture plug-in (research agent) would fill this.
8. **Policy.** The Indie Stone's Modding Policy (2.4) forbids selling access to mods. Cyrus can charge for the tool, but the community/mod store must keep Zomboid mods free to download, credit forks (4.1–4.3), and never label a mod "official" (2.2.3). Owner should confirm the community agent's store design respects this.

## Project Zomboid modding in one page (also for the marketing page)

**No loader to install.** Project Zomboid reads mods itself. A mod is a folder with a `mod.info` (id, name, version) and a `media/` folder of Lua scripts and plain-text "script" files that define items, recipes, vehicles and sounds. The game runs Lua 5.1 through Kahlua, a Java implementation, and exposes most of its Java classes to Lua.

**Build 42 is a different game for modders.** Build 42 became the default on 29 July 2026 (42.20; 42.21 is current, Build 41 lives on in the `legacy41` beta). Mods now sit in a version folder (`42/`) next to a `common/` folder for big shared assets; items declare `ItemType = base:weapon`; names, recipes and options are translated through UTF-8 JSON files; tags and weapon categories are registry ids like `base:screwdriver`. Almost every tutorial on the internet is for Build 41, which is why generic AI output breaks here and why Cyrus checks every file against the Build 42 rules first.

**Three Lua folders.** `shared` runs everywhere, `client` on each player's game (UI, keys, what the player sees), `server` on the server (and in singleplayer). Cyrus keeps all game-changing logic on the server: since multiplayer returned in 42.13, items and health that a client changes on its own are thrown away. Players' games detect a trigger and ask the server; the server checks distance, cooldowns and what the player is holding before anything happens.

**Everyone needs the mod.** Unlike a Minecraft plugin, a Zomboid mod runs on the server and on every player's PC, and the files must match. Servers list Workshop ids in `WorkshopItems=` and mod ids in `Mods=`; players then download the mods automatically when they join.

**How mods break.** A new build renames an API (the 42.21 stats system, for example), a Build 41 mod lands on a Build 42 server, two mods ship a file at the same path, or client-side code fights the server. Cyrus pins every mod to a minimum build, uses per-mod folders, puts every number behind a sandbox option with an on/off switch, and flags mods that a new game build may have broken.

**How to tune them.** Every generated mod adds its own page under Sandbox Options, so a server owner can change power, cooldowns, chances or turn the mod off without touching code; keybinds live under Options > Mods.

**Safety.** In April 2026 fourteen malicious Workshop mods wrote files outside the game folder; the game then removed and later restored `loadstring`. Cyrus blocks code-from-strings, file access, reflection, save deletion, admin and Steam-identity calls and obfuscated text before a mod is ever shown.
