"use strict";
// Static safety scan for generated plugins. Two layers:
//   1. bytecode: `javap -c -p` over every compiled class, matched against
//      invoked owners/methods (cannot be dodged by source formatting tricks);
//   2. source: heuristics that need string literals / context (paths, UUIDs,
//      name checks feeding privileges, encoded blobs).
// Verdict is decided here, never by the model.

const { execFileSync } = require("child_process");
const fs = require("fs");
const path = require("path");

// [id, regex over javap output, plain-English message]
// The scan reads `javap -c -p -v`: the whole constant pool, not only call instructions, so method references,
// lambda handles (`Runtime.getRuntime()::exec` shows up as `REF_invokeVirtual java/lang/Runtime.exec`) and
// string constants that name a class are all seen. Anything that can run other code, reach a network, or
// load code we can't check is a BLOCK for every build (there is no networking wrapper yet, so all of java.net
// that can touch the network is blocked, not only the obvious sockets).
const NET_VALUE_TYPES = "URI|URISyntaxException|URLEncoder|URLDecoder|InetAddress|Inet4Address|Inet6Address|InetSocketAddress|SocketAddress|MalformedURLException|UnknownHostException";
const REFLECT_DATA_TYPES = "Modifier|Array|Type|ParameterizedType|GenericArrayType|TypeVariable|WildcardType";
const BYTECODE_BLOCK = [
  ["exec", /java\/lang\/(Runtime\.exec|ProcessBuilder|ProcessHandle|Process\b)|java\/awt\/Desktop/, "runs other programs on the server machine"],
  ["network", new RegExp(`java/net/(?!(?:${NET_VALUE_TYPES})\\b)[A-Z]|java/net/http/|java/nio/channels/(Async\\w*)?(Socket|ServerSocket|Datagram)Channel|javax/net/|jdk/net/|java/net/spi/`), "connects to the internet or other machines"],
  ["dns", /java\/net\/InetAddress\.(getByName|getAllByName|getLocalHost|getCanonicalHostName|isReachable)|java\/net\/InetSocketAddress\."<init>":\(Ljava\/lang\/String;I\)V/, "looks up internet names (a way to leak data through DNS)"],
  ["jndi-rmi-jmx", /javax\/naming\/|java\/rmi\/|javax\/rmi\/|javax\/management\/|java\/sql\/DriverManager|javax\/sql\//, "reaches other services through naming, RMI, JMX or database lookups"],
  ["resolver", /org\/apache\/(maven|http)\/|org\/eclipse\/aether\/|org\/eclipse\/jgit\//, "downloads code or files through a bundled resolver"],
  ["classload", /java\/lang\/ClassLoader\.(defineClass|loadClass|findClass|getSystemClassLoader|getPlatformClassLoader)|java\/lang\/Thread\.(get|set)ContextClassLoader|java\/net\/URLClassLoader|MethodHandles\$Lookup\.(defineClass|defineHiddenClass)|java\/lang\/invoke\/MethodHandleProxies|java\/lang\/instrument\/|java\/lang\/ModuleLayer|java\/lang\/module\/|java\/lang\/Module\.add\w+/, "loads code at runtime that we can't check"],
  ["reflection", new RegExp(`java/lang/reflect/(?!(?:${REFLECT_DATA_TYPES})\\b)[A-Z]|java/lang/Class\\.(forName|getDeclared\\w+|getMethods?|getFields?|getConstructors?|newInstance|getEnclosingMethod|getNestHost)|java/lang/invoke/MethodHandles\\.(lookup|privateLookupIn)|java/lang/invoke/MethodHandle\\.invoke|MethodHandles\\$Lookup\\.(find\\w+|unreflect\\w*|in|lookupClass)\\b|java/lang/invoke/(VarHandle|MethodHandleInfo)`), "uses reflection or dynamic invocation, which can hide what the code really does"],
  ["deserialize-beans", /java\/io\/ObjectInput(Stream)?\b|java\/beans\/|java\/util\/ServiceLoader|javax\/xml\/(ws|bind)\/|java\/util\/jar\/(JarFile|JarInputStream)|java\/util\/zip\/ZipInputStream/, "decodes objects, beans or archives that can run code"],
  ["unsafe", /(?<![\w$])(sun|com\/sun|jdk\/(?!net)\w+)\//, "uses unsafe JVM internals"],

For the registry itself, I'm weighing a single JSON file that the scaffolder upserts into by game id, keeping it idempotent, versus generating per-game files that need static imports. For testing, I'm thinking the scaffolder should run against the real repo tree for a fake game id, then validate the generated adapter by dynamically importing it and running the validation functions directly rather than spinning up a full tsc pass.

For the type-check step, I'm leaning toward using the TypeScript compiler API to create a narrow program targeting just the generated files with the repo's tsconfig, so it type-checks only those files and their imports rather than the whole project, keeping the test fast while still proving correctness through a full manual tsc + seam/adapter test run when needed.

For the capability manifest, I'll derive capabilities from the adapter at runtime via a pure function rather than hardcoding them, while the record stores declared studio intent (initially all hidden with a "planned: phase 2" reason), and the health check enforces that declared capabilities never exceed what the adapter actually supports.

For languages and extra tooling on Valheim, I'm settling on BepInEx 5 with Harmony targeting netstandard2.1, and extra apps including the Unity editor, SteamCMD for downloading game DLLs at build time, a publicizer, and r2modman on the player side. Moving to Zomboid, PNG textures and clothing are viable for the texture studio exporter, sound uses ogg script definitions, models are FBX/X format which the model studio doesn't support, animation sets are hidden XML, sandbox config is a good target for the config studio, Lua emitters have a template, and test flight runs through SteamCMD with console log grepping plus Lua unit testing via busted, with Lua 5.1, PZ script files, and JSON translations as the core languages. Now starting on Hytale, noting its pixel textures reuse the pixel studio while sound format remains uncertain.

For Hytale, I'm working out that models and animations use new .blockymodel/.blockyanim formats with unpublished schemas, config runs through JSON assets with an in-game Asset Editor, designer plugins use a new Java 25 API, and test flight is blocked by OAuth device authentication requirements per server despite having a headless downloader and QUIC networking — a real automation obstacle; the Blockbench plugin is GPL-licensed so I shouldn't embed it. Then for FiveM/RedM, I'm noting textures need DDS conversion via a Windows worker, sound and model formats are mostly hidden or GPL-restricted so no new mesh support, animations rely on existing dictionaries, config goes through fxmanifest and server.cfg, designer emitters would need new Lua/C#/JS support with JS not yet in the language union, and test flight requires a Cfx.re license key to boot the server, with Lua 5.4, C#, and JavaScript as the core languages.

I'm also flagging several cross-game contract gaps: the language union is missing JavaScript and versioned runtimes like Java 25; the ArtifactRoute set is too Minecraft-specific and needs generic routes like serverMod, assetPack, and workshopItem; AssetKind is missing animation and material types with no sound or UI format fields; the delivery vocabulary is split between two inconsistent enums that should be unified; and the test lane assumes local hardware boot, which breaks down for Hytale's OAuth and FiveM's license key requirements.

Other findings: install side treats Valheim as single-valued when it's archetype-dependent on both sides; there are two separate knowledge systems (version-sheets vs knowledge-pack); template generators live outside the adapter with no link back to it; and the Minecraft adapter marking texture/sound delivery as "planned" is arguably honest since the relevant flags are off, but needs to flip to "available" once pack delivery goes live — a launch checklist item. Now I'm checking which studios actually have Minecraft record emitters (texture, sound, model, motion).

Working through each studio's derived availability for Minecraft — texture and sound planned, model planned, motion usable, config usable, datapack and designers depend on route/plugin availability, creatures planned, library usable, testflight tied to boot availability — I realize I need a general notion of "route availability" that governs whether a studio state is usable vs planned vs none, rather than treating each ad hoc. I'm restructuring adapterNeed to return an object with ok/why plus an optional availability string and reason, then rewriting the manifest logic to use this consistently across studios.

File format (YAML, JSON, .cfg, Lua tables, ini), where it lives, reload behaviour, who wins (server or client).

## 6. Networking
What the server pushes to players (assets? code?), what needs every client to install, version matching (network
version), cross-play / console limits.

## 7. Packaging and install
Package shape (jar, dll, zip, pak, folder + manifest), install path on a dedicated server, restart or hot reload,
dependency handling, how Nxeon's installer for this game works today (`lib/mods/installers/*`).

## 8. Update / outdated signals and version cadence
Patch cadence (weekly, monthly), how breaking changes are announced, a machine-readable source to poll
(Steam build id, GitHub releases, Maven metadata), the exact log line a broken mod prints.

Mod sites (Workshop, Thunderstore, CurseForge, Modrinth, own hub), their AI-content and disclosure rules, licence
habits, what gets a mod banned, monetisation norms.

| Document | URL | Retrieved | Key clauses (quote, short) | Label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EULA / ToS | | | | |
| Mod policy | | | | |
| AI-generated content | | | | |

| Monetisation | | | | |

official downloader, account needed?), RAM / CPU, the log line that proves a mod loaded, a console / RCON channel for
functional checks, what only a real client can show.

# {{GAME_NAME}} ({{GAME_ID}}): asset sourcing report

Playbook {{PLAYBOOK_VERSION}}, phase 5. Date {{DATE}}. Rules: CC0 only by default (CC-BY tier only after the owner's
attribution decision); read every licence on the source's own page and quote it; aggregator labels are never trusted;
API terms obeyed (no scraping where an API or robots.txt forbids it); staging only (`/tank/cyrus-library-staging/`,
never git, never the prod DB). Reuse first: the shared library already holds ~61k CC0/CC-BY items
(research J-asset-library-ingest.md, S-motion-assets.md); only fetch what this game needs that the library lacks.

## What this game can use (from `assetProfile.catalog.accepts`)
| Catalog kind | native / convert / none | Converter that exists today | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|

## Already in the shared library that fits
Run the fit (lib/cyrus/library/v2/fit.ts) on a sample: counts of good / ok / no by kind, with the top no-reasons.

## New sources
| Source | Licence quote + url | Retrieved | Kind: count | Size | Decision (in / out / owner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Game-derived content (never public)
- Base meshes, textures, sounds of the game are **game-derived**: job retention only, never stored beyond the job,
  never in any library, never redistributed. A retexture ships the delta, never the base.
- BYO-assets flow: the user supplies their own template / base file, attests ownership, Cyrus works on it in the job.

## Ledger rows
Append to the staging ledger (`LICENCE-LEDGER.csv` pattern): source, pack, licence, quote, url, retrieved, decision.

## Ingestion plan
1. Stage files + `catalog.jsonl` rows (sha256 ids, dedupe).
2. Measure: `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/catalog-stage-a.ts --catalog catalog.jsonl --cc0-only --out report.json` (no model calls).
3. Throwaway import: `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/library-import.ts --entries entries.jsonl --dry-run` then `--pg --twice` on the node-2 `wt_*` DB only.
4. Owner gate G5-assets before anything leaves staging.

## Owner decisions

# {{GAME_NAME}} ({{GAME_ID}}): legal + security checklist

Playbook {{PLAYBOOK_VERSION}}, phase 7 (legal facts gathered in phases 0-1). An agent fills the facts; only the owner
(or counsel) decides and flips `assetProfile.legal.reviewed` (gate G7-legal). Quote short excerpts with url + date.

## Legal
- [ ] EULA / ToS read in full (not a summary). URL + retrieval date:
- [ ] Mods allowed? Distribution allowed? Who owns a mod? Licence granted back to the publisher?
- [ ] Commercial: may a third party sell a mod-creation service / tool? May mods be sold, or only free?
- [ ] AI-generated content: any clause? Disclosure required by the mod sites (Thunderstore, Workshop, CurseForge)?
- [ ] Redistribution: may a mod contain any game file? (default: never; `redistributeBase: false`)
- [ ] Hosting terms: may Nxeon host servers for customers (provider programme, licence keys, entitlements, server caps)?
- [ ] Monetisation rules for servers (cosmetics, gambling, authorised partners only)
- [ ] Trademark: may we use the game name on marketing pages? Logos only from the owner's own art
- [ ] Policy change watch: where to re-read, how often (quarterly default)
- [ ] `commercialOk` / `aiOk` stay "unknown" until a reviewer read the source; `attestationRequired` true when the user supplies game files

## Security: threat model delta
- [ ] New language / runtime: what a generated mod can reach (files, network, processes, reflection, native code)
- [ ] Dangerous API list in GameSupport + scanner (block / warn), tested with negative cases
- [ ] New tools run on user data only inside a sandbox: no network, read-only fs, caps, timeouts, unprivileged user
- [ ] Windows worker (if any): ephemeral VM per job, pull-based queue, signed job manifest, no credentials on the guest, outputs re-scanned on Linux
- [ ] Imports of user mods: zip limits, path traversal, symlinks, quarantine (reuse lib/cyrus/import rules)
- [ ] Delivery: what a bad mod can do to a customer server (restart loops, world corruption) and the rollback path
- [ ] Test Flight sandbox: loopback only, own netns, random secrets, no customer data
- [ ] Second-agent adversarial pass (pattern: research AC-security-audit.md); findings fixed or listed with severity

## Owner sign-off
- G7-legal signed by: ____ on ____ ; notes:

# {{GAME_NAME}} ({{GAME_ID}}): verification plan

Playbook {{PLAYBOOK_VERSION}}, phases 4 + 6. Principle: a check counts only if it RAN. Compile, scan, boot and
functional test are separate checks; a skipped required check means the flight is not a pass.

## Lanes
| Check | Tool / command | Where it runs | Pass condition | Status (not built / built / running) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Validator (static) | `lib/cyrus/games/{{GAME_ID}}.validate.ts` | anywhere (pure) | zero blocking issues | |
| Compile | | node-2 via devhost | artifact produced | |
| Safety scan | | node-2 | no block findings | |
| Boot (headless server) | | node-2 container, loopback only | server reaches ready line | |
| Loaded | log line: | | the mod's own load line, no errors | |
| Functional | console / RCON / bot | | scripted checks answer as expected | |
| Clean stop + no leaks | | | server stops, no stray files | |
| Real client | a human | own PC | each archetype seen working | |

## Headless boot recipe
Download (anonymous SteamCMD app id / official downloader / account?), image, RAM / CPU per run, start command,
ready line, how the mod is installed, timeout, teardown. Never on the primary, never on a customer VM.

## Eval set
`services/modbuilder/eval/games/{{GAME_ID}}.jsonl`: 30 prompts across the game's categories (simple / standard /
complex) + 10 adversarial (network, file deletion, admin abuse, cheats, obfuscation) that must be refused.
Score per prompt: validator pass, compile pass, load pass, functional pass. Paid model runs need the owner's budget.

## Evidence to record (record.json `evidence`)
- templateValidated: { ref, at }
- compile / eval / flight: { ref, at, passed, total } (measured, never estimated; >= 10 samples before a rate is shown)
- realClientDay, legalReviewed: { ref, at }

planned -> template -> beta -> stable; exact exit criteria in PLAYBOOK.md "Maturity ladder".

# Common rules for every onboarding agent (paste at the end of every brief)

Model rule (owner, 2026-10-10): **Sonnet** for research passes and small items, **Opus** for big build items, few agents.
Every brief below already names its model. One agent per area; never two agents on the same files.

## Frugality
- **Reuse before research.** First read the game's `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` files and grep
  `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` for the game name. Never re-fetch a page an existing report already cites unless
  you are re-verifying a U-labelled claim.
- Page budget per research area: about 10 pages fetched, 15 searches. Stop early when the answer is clear.
- Official sources first (the loader's docs, source repo, LICENSE files via the GitHub API, release feeds). Host
  wikis and blogs are secondary: label them, do not chain them.
- Report under 400 words unless the brief says otherwise; tables over prose; no repetition of the brief.
- **No paid model calls** (eval runs, image or 3D generation APIs) without the owner's explicit budget.

## Honesty
- Label every claim **V** (url fetched + date), **V-s** (search snippet only) or **U** (unverified). Unlabelled = bug.
- "Not found" is an answer. Never invent numbers, prices, limits, stats or quotes. Estimates say "estimate".
- A status ("built", "tested", "supported") only for something that actually ran; say what ran and what did not.
- `legal.reviewed`, `commercialOk`, `aiOk` stay false / "unknown": only the owner flips them.

## Safety (hard rules)
- Never edit or build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there. Work in your own worktree
  under `/tank/dev-worktrees/`.
- Heavy commands only through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost` (tsc, tests, builds, game servers): one heavy job at a time,
  node-2 agent memory ~7-10 GB. Never on the primary.
- Never `git add -A` / `git add .`; add only the files you changed. Commits end with the attribution line you were given.
- Never `pkill` / `killall` by pattern; stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by your own PID.
- Never deploy, never touch production, the build VM (88001), customer servers or customer VMs.
- Never run database role / ownership commands (`REASSIGN OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, roles), on any cluster.
- Never copy secrets or `.env` files anywhere; never print them.
- Game binaries, decompiled code and game assets never enter git; only distilled facts do.
- Downloads of game server software only into a throwaway sandbox on node-2, by the official anonymous method, and
  only after the owner allowed it for this game.
- HOST SEAM: no new imports of Nxeon internals under `lib/cyrus` (`test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts`).
- Flag nothing on. Registering an adapter, flipping a catalog status or a setting is an owner gate.
- Never reply to customers or send email; draft only.

## Hand-off
Write your report to the path the brief gives (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<topic>.md`) and update the
game's onboarding files (`TODO.md` boxes you completed, `record.json` `research` list). Final reply: what ran, what did
not, open owner decisions.

# Agent briefs: phase 1 deep research (Sonnet, one pass per area)

Each brief is self-contained. Run at most two in parallel, on different areas; each writes ONE section of
`docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/RESEARCH.md` (the section number is in the brief) plus its own short report.
Replace `<GAME>`, `<id>`, `<CODE>`; append COMMON-RULES.md. Bundling: small games may run R1+R2+R7 as one pass,
R3+R4 as one pass, R5+R6 as one pass (three agents instead of nine).

## R1 Languages, runtimes, mod loaders (RESEARCH.md sections 1 + 2)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> mod LANGUAGES, RUNTIMES and LOADERS for Cyrus. Reuse first: SCORECARD.md and any
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research file naming <GAME>. Questions: mod language + exact version; runtime that loads it;
compiler / build tool and its licence + OS; official API vs community loader(s), who maintains them, licence (read the
LICENSE via the GitHub API), version pairing loader <-> game, where the API reference lives (javadoc / typings /
decompiled only). Which loader do Nxeon servers of this game run (check lib/mods/installers/ and lib/*-image.ts in the
repo)? Does GameSupport.language (Java | C# | Lua | C++ | JSON/data) cover it; if not, say so (contract gap).
Label V / V-s / U. Budget 10 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r1.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R2 Asset formats (RESEARCH.md section 3)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> ASSET FORMATS for Cyrus studios: mesh, texture (channels, colour space, compression,
max resolution), material / shader, sound (codec, channels, sample rate, length limits), UI (images, fonts, layout).
For each: format, limits, authoring tool + licence + OS, and whether Cyrus can WRITE it on Linux without the game
installed. Compare against lib/cyrus/adapters/asset-profile.ts fields (TextureCompression, ChannelRole, EngineFamily)
and research H-3d-games.md section 3 (per-engine packing) so you do not redo engine-level facts.
Label V / V-s / U. Budget 10 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r2.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R3 Animation / motion (RESEARCH.md section 4)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> ANIMATION and EFFECTS: skeletal / keyframe / procedural, file formats, who drives
playback (server packets or client scripts), tick rate, particles / VFX format, sound sync. Map each to the Cyrus
motion core track kinds (transform, particle, sound, material, event) as native / approx / none, and node kinds
(bone, part, socket, hinge, wheel, seat, emitter). Reuse research R-motion-effects.md section 3 (per-game table).
Label V / V-s / U. Budget 8 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r3.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R4 Config, networking, packaging, install (RESEARCH.md sections 5, 6, 7)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> CONFIG conventions (format, location, reload, who wins), NETWORKING (what the server
pushes to players, what needs every client, version / network-version matching, console / cross-play limits) and
PACKAGING + INSTALL (package shape, dedicated-server install path, restart vs hot reload, dependencies). Read how
Nxeon installs mods for this game today (lib/mods/installers/<game>.ts, worker/game-mods.ts) and say what Cyrus can
reuse. Label V / V-s / U. Budget 10 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r4.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R5 Versions, cadence, outdated signals (RESEARCH.md section 8)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> VERSION CADENCE (last 12 months of patches with dates), how breaking changes are
announced, a MACHINE-READABLE source to poll (Steam build id via the public API, GitHub releases, Maven metadata, news
feed), the exact log lines a broken / outdated mod prints, and the loader's own version checks. Output a draft
GameSupport.versions + outdatedSignals block. Label V / V-s / U. Budget 8 pages.
Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r5.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R6 Community norms (RESEARCH.md section 9)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research <GAME> COMMUNITY NORMS: the main mod sites, their rules on AI-generated mods and disclosure,
licence habits, what gets a mod removed, monetisation norms, notable malicious-mod incidents (and what the game did).
Label V / V-s / U. Budget 8 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r6.md (<= 250 words).
```

## R7 Legal facts (RESEARCH.md section 10; the owner decides)
```
Model: Sonnet. Collect <GAME> LEGAL FACTS for the owner: EULA / ToS, mod policy, AI-content clauses, server-hosting /
provider terms (licence keys, provider programmes, server caps), monetisation rules, trademark use. Fetch the full
pages (not summaries); quote short excerpts with url + retrieval date; say which pages could not be fetched (403) and
were read only through secondary sources. Do NOT conclude "allowed": list facts and open questions. Fill
docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/LEGAL.md "Legal" boxes with facts only. Budget 10 pages.
Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r7.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R8 Verification lane (RESEARCH.md section 11)
```
Model: Sonnet. Research how to boot a <GAME> DEDICATED SERVER HEADLESS on Linux in a container for Cyrus Test Flight:
download method (anonymous SteamCMD app id, official downloader, account / licence key needed?), Docker images used by
hosts (licence), RAM / CPU / disk per run, start command, the READY log line, how a mod is installed and the line that
proves it loaded, a console / RCON / REST channel for functional checks, what only a real client can verify. Do NOT
download or run anything. Reuse lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts (Minecraft lane) as the shape.
Label V / V-s / U. Budget 8 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r8.md (<= 300 words).
```

## R9 Asset sources for the library (phase 5 input)
```
Model: Sonnet. Find CC0 asset sources that fit <GAME> (style, formats from assetProfile.catalog), beyond what the
shared library already holds (read research J-asset-library-ingest.md and S-motion-assets.md first: ~61k items,
mostly low-poly / stylised, CC0). Read every licence on the source's own page and quote it; reject aggregator-only
claims; respect API terms and robots.txt. Do NOT download. Fill docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/ASSETS.md
"New sources" table. Budget 10 pages. Report /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/<CODE>-<id>-r9.md (<= 300 words).
```

input.content:
# Cyrus game onboarding playbook

Playbook version: **1.0.0** (2026-10-11). Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Lessons: [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md).
Owner brief 2026-10-11: onboarding a new game must be flawless and repeatable, and this document keeps improving.
Minecraft is the reference implementation. Hytale and FiveM/RedM are ON HOLD and appear only as worked case studies
([CASE-STUDIES.md](CASE-STUDIES.md)).

This is a living document. It changes only through the loop in [How this playbook stays current](#how-this-playbook-stays-current).

## Start here

```
npx tsx scripts/cyrus/new-game.ts <gameId> --name "Game Name" [--language Lua] [--engine unity]
```
The scaffolder writes the skeleton (adapter at maturity `planned`, GameSupport stub, empty knowledge pack, eval-set
stub, onboarding record, checklist and doc stubs) and **registers nothing**: no adapter in `ADAPTERS`, no catalog row,
no flag. It is idempotent (an existing file is never overwritten). `--docs-only` writes only
`docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (use it for screening, before anyone writes code). `--manifest` prints the derived
capability manifest. Then work through `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` phase by phase.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/record.json` | phase, status, declared maturity, **evidence**, emitters, owner gate signatures, research reused |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` | the checklist (parsed by `lib/cyrus/onboarding/todo.ts`, shown on `/admin/cyrus/games`) |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/*.md` | the filled templates: SCORECARD, RESEARCH, CAPABILITY, ADAPTER, ASSETS, LEGAL, VERIFICATION, LAUNCH |
| `lib/cyrus/onboarding/` | types (phases, gates, ladder), `health.ts` (ladder exit criteria + record checks), `manifest.ts` (derived capability manifest), `todo.ts`, `records.server.ts` |
| `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` | onboarding health over every record, docs coverage, scaffolder end to end |
| `templates/` | the templates the scaffolder copies, and `templates/agent-briefs/` |

## Principles (non-negotiable)
1. **Delivery first.** A game fits Cyrus only if what we build reaches players without each player installing it by
   hand, or the product is honest that it is a download (research H: "a delivery problem first").
2. **Evidence over claims.** A maturity, a pass rate, a "supported" exists only if it ran and is recorded with a date.
   The onboarding health test fails a record that claims more than its evidence.
3. **Reuse before research.** Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` and the case studies first. Never pay twice for
   the same page. Every record lists the research it reused.
4. **Honest unknowns.** Every fact is labelled V / V-s / U; an unknown stays in `GameSupport.unknowns` until verified.
5. **Game files never ship.** `redistributeBase: false` always; game-derived content is job-only and never enters a
   library; game binaries and decompiled code never enter git.
6. **Host seam.** New Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through `lib/cyrus/host` (`test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts`).
7. **Flag nothing on.** Registration, catalog status, settings and deploys are owner gates.
8. **One heavy job at a time** on node-2 through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost`; nothing heavy on the primary.

## Roles
| Role | Who | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | the owner only | signs the gates below; decides legal, money, flags, launch |
| Research agent | Sonnet, one pass per area | phases 0, 1, 5 (sources), 6 runs, 7 adversarial read |
| Build agent | Opus, few agents, one owner per file | phases 2, 3 (proposal), 4, 8 |
| Reviewer | a second agent | adversarial security pass, research spot-check of U labels |

Agent briefs with frugality and safety rules baked in: [templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md](templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md),
[SCREENING](templates/agent-briefs/SCREENING.md), [RESEARCH](templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md) (R1-R9, one per area),
[BUILD](templates/agent-briefs/BUILD.md) (B1-B5), [REVIEW](templates/agent-briefs/REVIEW.md) (verification run,
adversarial pass, lessons learned).

## Owner gates
| Gate | Phase | The owner signs that |
|---|---|---|
| **G0-go** | 0 | the screening verdict is accepted (GO, or LATER / NO with the reason) |
| **G1-research** | 1 | the research report is accepted (unknowns listed, nothing invented) |
| **G3-tooling** | 3 | new apps, workers, licences and costs are approved |
| **G5-assets** | 5 | the asset sources and the licence ledger are approved |
| **G6-beta** | 6 | the maturity bump to beta is approved (evidence attached) |
| **G7-legal** | 7 | the EULA / mod policy / AI terms were read; `legal.reviewed` flips |
| **G8-flags** | 8 | the flag order and plan gating are approved |
| **G9-launch** | 9 | the game goes `live` in the catalog |

A gate is signed by writing `{ "by": "<owner>", "at": "<ISO date>" }` into `record.json` `gates` and ticking the
`OWNER GATE` line in `TODO.md`. Agents never sign. Games whose work predates this playbook carry `retrofit: true`:
missing early gates are warnings, never back-filled signatures.

```
 P0 screen --G0--> P1 research --G1--> P2 capability --> P3 tooling --G3--> P4 knowledge+build
      |                                                                        |
      +--> LATER / NO (status on-hold / rejected, holdReason)                  v
 P9 launch+upkeep <--G9-- P8 integration <--G8-- P7 legal <--G7-- P6 verify <--G6-- P5 assets <--G5--+
```
P5 can run in parallel with P3/P4 (different files, different agent). P7 legal facts are gathered from P0 on; the
owner's review closes it.

---

## Phase 0 Screening
**Purpose:** a cheap go / no-go before anyone researches deeply. **Budget:** one Sonnet pass, about 10 pages.
**Entry:** a game name. **Template:** [templates/SCREENING-SCORECARD.md](templates/SCREENING-SCORECARD.md).

| # | Criterion | Weight | Knockout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delivery path to players | 20 | K1: manual client install only -> at most LATER |
| 2 | Mod policy / EULA / AI + commercial terms | 15 | K2: mods or paid mod services forbidden -> NO |
| 3 | Server availability + fit on Nxeon hosting | 15 | K3: no dedicated server -> NO for hosting |
| 4 | Formats and toolchain: licences + OS | 10 | |
| 5 | Asset-redistribution constraints | 10 | K4: a mod must contain game files -> NO |
| 6 | AI feasibility | 10 | |
| 7 | Audience / demand (sourced numbers only) | 15 | |
| 8 | Maintenance burden | 5 | |

Each criterion scores 0-5; total = sum(weight x score / 5), out of 100. **Recommended threshold: GO at 65+, LATER at
50-64, NO under 50**, knockouts override. Two or more U-labelled criteria of weight 15+ cap the verdict at LATER.
The verdict names the **narrowest viable first lane** (e.g. "server plugins only", "texture-only on user templates").

**Exit:** scorecard filled with labelled sources; verdict + first lane + revisit trigger; record status set
(`active`, or `on-hold` / `rejected` with `holdReason`). **Gate G0-go.**

## Phase 1 Deep research
**Purpose:** every fact the adapter needs, verified. **Template:** [templates/RESEARCH-REPORT.md](templates/RESEARCH-REPORT.md).
**Briefs:** R1-R9 in [templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md](templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md) (bundle into three passes for small games).

Research areas (one section each in RESEARCH.md): languages and runtimes; mod loaders / APIs; asset formats (mesh,
texture, material, sound, animation, UI); animation / motion system; config conventions; networking; packaging and
install; update / outdated signals; version cadence; community norms; legal; verification lane.

Rules: official sources first (loader docs, source repos, LICENSE via the GitHub API, release feeds); host wikis are
secondary and labelled; a page that returns 403 is reported as such (Hytale's support pages did) and the claim stays
V-s; "not found" is a valid answer.

**Exit:** every RESEARCH.md section answered or explicitly unknown; contract gaps against the shared types listed;
ranked unknowns + owner decisions. **Gate G1-research.**

## Phase 2 Capability mapping
**Purpose:** turn research into the typed contract and decide what Cyrus can honestly offer.
**Templates:** [templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md](templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md), [templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md](templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md). **Brief:** B1.

1. Fill `lib/cyrus/games/<id>.ts` (GameSupport: versions, install, verification, dangerous APIs, breakage risks,
   outdated signals, categories, sources, unknowns).
2. Fill `lib/cyrus/adapters/<id>.ts` (GameAdapter: artifacts with honest availability, toolchain, knowledge ref,
   versions, assetDelivery per kind, install, testLane, routeRules with honest limit messages). Maturity stays `planned`.
3. Fill the AssetProfile (formats, channel map, colour spaces, normal convention, max resolution, UV + skeleton policy,
   packaging, delivery strategy, worker class, required game files, legal with `reviewed: false`, validators, preview
   shader, catalog fit hints, motion capability). `validateAssetProfile()` must return no issues.
4. **Derive the capability manifest** (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/manifest.ts`, `new-game.ts <id> --manifest`): for each
   studio / tool (Texture, Sound, Model, Motion, Config, Data Pack studios; designers; creatures; library fit; import;
   Mod Packs + conflicts; Test Flight; install onto Nxeon servers; Server Doctor) the state **usable** (adapter supports
   it + a game emitter exists + its delivery / route is available), **planned** (something is missing, with the reason)
   or **hidden** (the game cannot use it; never shown to customers). Plus route availability, worker classes
   (linux-cpu / windows-tools / gpu), required game files (none / user-supplied / platform-licensed) and the **legal
   class per asset type** from the ledger (`lib/cyrus/assets3d/ledger.ts`; game-derived = job-only, never in a library).
5. List **contract gaps**: anything the shared types cannot express (see the cross-game list in CASE-STUDIES.md).
   Raise them; do not work around them silently.

**Exit:** files typed and validated; worksheet agrees with the derived manifest; contract gaps listed; health test green.

## Phase 3 Tooling decisions
**Purpose:** decide, per studio and artifact, what has to be brought in, before anyone builds it.

Decision tree (per studio / artifact in the worksheet):
```
Can an existing Cyrus studio produce it (the neutral core: textures as lossless channel layers, glTF + sidecar,
MotionSpec, ConfigSpec)?
 |- yes, and the game reads the format directly ............ EMITTER ONLY (a lowering/export in the adapter's lane)
 |- yes, but the game needs a different container/encoding .. EXPORTER + CONVERTER (pick a library, licence check)
 |- no: new language / compiler ............................ NEW TOOLCHAIN (build-host package, sandboxed compile)
 |- no: game-specific authoring tool ........................ NEW APP / WORKER (licence, OS, sandbox, cost) or HIDE
 '- no free / licensable tool exists ........................ HIDE the studio for this game (state = hidden)
```
**Licence check** (read the tool's own LICENSE, via the GitHub API when it is a repo):
| Licence | Rule |
|---|---|
| MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 / zlib | ok in workers and libraries |
| GPL / LGPL | run only as a **separate process** on user data; never link, embed or ship it (Blockbench, Sollumz) |
| none declared / "NOASSERTION" | legal review first (CodeWalker, Crowbar) |
| closed / proprietary EULA | no, unless the owner licenses it explicitly |
| community licence with region or use limits | no (Hunyuan3D excludes EU/UK/KR) |

**Sandbox + isolation:** every tool that touches user data runs as an unprivileged user with no network, a read-only
filesystem except a tmpfs work dir, CPU / memory / time caps and outputs re-validated by a Linux validator (pattern:
the meshgen Blender sandbox and Test Flight's loopback netns, research AC).

**Windows worker rules** (only when a Windows-only tool is unavoidable): ephemeral VM per job (or snapshot revert);
pull-based job queue; signed job manifest; allow-listed tools only; no outbound network except the broker; no Proxmox
or Nxeon credentials on the guest; hard timeout and caps; outputs returned through object storage and **re-scanned on
Linux**; a platform-licensed game install never lives on it without a separate legal review (`validateAssetProfile`
`windows_licensed`). The first game that needs it is the forcing function that proves the worker; no Windows fleet.

**Cost:** compute per build (node-2 minutes), storage per tenant, licence fees, model tokens per build (estimate,
labelled), owner time for real-client days.

**Exit:** every planned / hidden studio has a decision; every new tool has licence + sandbox + cost; the emitters
list in `record.json` names what will exist. **Gate G3-tooling.**

## Phase 4 Knowledge + build
**Purpose:** make the AI write correct mods for this game and prove it with tools, not opinions. **Briefs:** B2, B3.

- **API sheet:** verified facts, one per line, tagged `[Type] ...` so retrieval can inject only what a plan touches
  (pattern: `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts`; Minecraft uses `services/modbuilder/sheets/<version>.md`).
- **Failure rules:** `detect` regex + `fix` hint + `why` (+ `autofix` when a deterministic rewrite exists).
- **Dangerous API list:** block / warn patterns in GameSupport and in the scanner / validator; negative tests for each.
- **Compiler / validator toolchain:** pinned versions, runs on node-2 via devhost, against public loader packages;
  game binaries only in a node-2 cache. A pure-TS validator for languages without a compiler (Zomboid's Lua lint).
- **Scan rules:** what the generated code may reach (files, network, processes, reflection, native code); Minecraft's
  `services/modbuilder/scan.js` is the model (bytecode + source).
- **Test Flight equivalent:** how to boot the dedicated server headless (download method, image, RAM/CPU, ready line,
  install step, the mod's own load line, a console / RCON / REST channel for functional checks, clean stop). Design it
  here, run it in phase 6. Minecraft: `lib/cyrus/testflight` + `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight`.
- **Eval set:** `services/modbuilder/eval/games/<id>.jsonl` with **at least 40 prompts**: 30 across the game's
  categories (simple / standard / complex) + 10 adversarial that must be refused (network, file deletion, admin abuse,
  cheats, obfuscation). No `todo` rows left. (Minecraft's lives in `services/modbuilder/eval/prompts.jsonl` + `sets/`;
  the per-game folder keeps new games out of the Minecraft loaders.)

**Exit:** template or real build output passes the validator (`evidence.templateValidated`); eval set complete;
Test Flight equivalent designed with its recipe in VERIFICATION.md.

## Phase 5 Assets for the library
**Purpose:** give the game's studios and builds a licence-clean starting library. **Template:** [templates/ASSET-SOURCING.md](templates/ASSET-SOURCING.md). **Brief:** R9.

- **Reuse first.** The shared library already holds ~61k CC0 / CC-BY items (10.3k models, 2.9k PBR sets, 1.4k HDRIs,
  38k sprites, 4.2k icons, 3.1k sounds; research J) plus ~2k motion items (research S). Run the per-game fit
  (`lib/cyrus/library/v2/fit.ts`, driven by `assetProfile.catalog`) before fetching anything new.
- **CC0 only by default.** CC-BY only after the owner's attribution decision (still open). Read every licence on the
  source's own page and quote it; never trust an aggregator label (Papyszoo's blanket "CC0" was wrong in places);
  watch for licence changes (Quaternius moved new packs to a no-redistribution licence on 2026-08-28).
- **Where to look by game type:** voxel / pixel games: Kenney 2D, game-icons, pixel packs, procedural (Texture Studio);
  stylised 3D: Quaternius, KayKit, Kenney 3D, Base Mesh; realistic 3D: Poly Haven, ambientCG, Smithsonian CC0 scans;
  sound: Kenney audio, BrainBytes / Ben Burnes, OpenGameArt CC0, FSD50K CC0 clips; motion: KayKit + Quaternius
  animation libraries, OGA CC0 flipbooks. Rejected sources stay rejected (Freesound scraping, Mixamo, Sonniss, ...;
  research J / S ledgers).
- **Game-derived content never public.** Base meshes, textures and sounds of the game are `game-derived`: job
  retention, never stored beyond the job, never in any library, never redistributed; a retexture ships the delta.
  **BYO-assets flow:** the user supplies their own template / base file with an ownership attestation
  (`attestationRequired`), Cyrus works on it inside the job, the deliverable carries only user content.
- **Ledger:** every staged item has a source / pack / licence / quote / url / retrieved row (`LICENCE-LEDGER.csv`).
- **Catalog fit fields:** `accepts` per kind (native / convert / none), `noneReasons`, `styleAffinity`, `triBudget`,
  `textureRes`, `audio` (format, channels, max seconds).
- **Ingestion with the existing scripts:** stage under `/tank/cyrus-library-staging/` (never git, never prod);
  measure with `scripts/cyrus/catalog-stage-a.ts --cc0-only`; import into the node-2 throwaway DB with
  `scripts/cyrus/library-import.ts --dry-run`, then `--pg --twice` (idempotency).

**Exit:** ASSETS.md filled; ledger rows for every new source; fit sample checked. **Gate G5-assets.**

## Phase 6 Verification
**Purpose:** measured evidence for the maturity claim. **Template:** [templates/VERIFICATION-PLAN.md](templates/VERIFICATION-PLAN.md). **Brief:** V1.

- **Flight tests:** headless boot + load line + functional checks + clean stop, on real server software in a node-2
  sandbox (loopback only, own netns, random secrets). A skipped required check is not a pass.
- **Real-client day:** a human with a real client joins and sees each archetype work (client-side features cannot be
  verified headless). Name the tester and the day.
- **Pass-rate evidence:** measured only, recorded in `record.json` `evidence` with ref + date + passed / total; no rate
  shown under 10 samples (`lib/cyrus/eval/passrate.ts` MIN_PUBLISH_N).

### Maturity ladder
The exit criteria are code (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/health.ts` LADDER_CRITERIA); the test checks this table matches.

| Rung | Exact exit criteria |
|---|---|
| planned | Nothing built. Adapter file + GameSupport stub + record exist; every unknown is listed. |
| template | Canned / template output exists and passes the game's validator. |
| beta | Real AI build path: compile >= 90% over >= 20 builds, the safety scan runs on every build, eval run >= 20 measured prompts at >= 80%; owner gate G6-beta signed. |
| stable | Beta plus headless boot + functional flights >= 95% over >= 10 flights, one real-client day, legal reviewed by the owner (G7-legal) and a no-manual delivery path. |

The adapter's `maturity` may never exceed the record's `declaredMaturity`, which may never exceed what the evidence
proves. **Exit:** evidence recorded; maturity bump proposed. **Gate G6-beta** (for beta).

## Phase 7 Legal + security review
**Template:** [templates/LEGAL-CHECKLIST.md](templates/LEGAL-CHECKLIST.md). **Briefs:** R7 (facts), S1 (adversarial pass).

Legal: EULA / ToS read in full; mod policy; AI-content terms and mod-site disclosure rules; redistribution (never base
files); hosting terms (provider programmes, licence keys, server caps: Hytale's Game Server Provider entitlement is the
example); monetisation; trademark. `commercialOk` / `aiOk` stay "unknown" until a reviewer read the source.
Security: threat model delta for the new language / runtime / tools / delivery path; dangerous-API tests; sandbox
review; Windows worker review if any; second-agent adversarial pass with VERIFIED-TEST / RUN / READ labels (research AC).

**Exit:** checklist complete, findings fixed or listed. **Gate G7-legal** (the owner flips `legal.reviewed`).

## Phase 8 Nxeon integration
**Brief:** B5. Every item behind a flag that defaults OFF. Touchpoints for a new game:

| Touchpoint | File(s) |
|---|---|
| Cyrus game registry (studio ring, version picker, marketing copy) | `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (stays `soon`), `lib/cyrus/data.ts` GAMES (logo from the owner's art under `public/cyrus/games/`) |
| Admin status override + "can be live" rule | `lib/cyrus/game-status.ts` (`CYRUS_BUILDABLE_GAMES` only with a real build pipeline) |
| Adapter registration (router, retexture export targets) | `lib/cyrus/adapters/index.ts` + the count in `test/cyrus-engine-core.test.ts`; `lib/cyrus/modelstudio/retex/export.ts` iterates ADAPTERS |
| Template generator (previews) | `lib/cyrus/engine/games/<id>.ts` |
| Categories | `lib/cyrus/categories.ts` |
| Nxeon game family + installer | `lib/games.ts` GAME_FAMILIES (the slug can differ: `projectzomboid` vs Cyrus `zomboid`), `lib/mods/installers/<game>.ts`, `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts` |
| Install paths, grants and scopes | server grants (`servers.read`, `inventory.read`, `files.write.mods`, `server.restart`, `logs.read.tail`, `pack.set`) via the host seam; paths regex-pinned |
| Delivery strategy | `lib/cyrus/delivery` (journal, rollback, health) for server-side installs; workshop / download flows are guidance, never auto-publish |
| Plan gating | `lib/cyrus/engine-core/asset-gate.ts` (studios per plan), `lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts` |
| Readiness + onboarding on admin | `docs/cyrus/readiness/<id>.md`, `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (both shown on `/admin/cyrus/games`) |
| Marketing "coming soon" -> live | customer-facing copy only, no invented stats; What's New only for customer-facing changes |

**Exit:** all touchpoints wired behind flags, adapter registered, flag order written. **Gate G8-flags.**

## Phase 9 Launch + upkeep
**Template:** [templates/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md](templates/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md).
Launch: maturity >= beta, health test green, gates G0-G8 signed, a real install on a Nxeon server of the game (owner /
test account) with restart, verify, uninstall and rollback, support macros drafted (never sent without approval),
docs/DOCUMENTATION.md updated, then the owner flips the catalog status. **Gate G9-launch.**
Deploys only through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` then `scripts/promote-production.sh` (owner / root).

Upkeep: patch watch (source + cadence + who), outdated signals wired to the lifecycle (`GameSupport.outdatedSignals`),
version-table bump procedure (registry + knowledge pack + failure rules + harness re-run), quarterly policy re-read
(`legal.retrievedAt`), monthly eval regression (budget-gated), support macros kept current.

**Exit (and the end of every onboarding, including abandoned ones):** lessons learned appended to LESSONS.md.

---

## Frugality rules
- One Sonnet pass per research area at about 10 pages; bundle areas for small games (three passes, not nine).
- Opus only for phase 2 / 4 / 8 build work; one owner per file; at most two agents at once per game.
- Reuse the case studies and the cross-game contract gap list; extend them, do not rewrite them.
- No paid model calls (eval runs, image / 3D APIs) without the owner's budget in the brief.
- Templates are cheap to fill on purpose: tables over prose, labels over paragraphs.

## How this playbook stays current
1. **Lessons learned after every onboarding.** The phase 9 exit (and any abandonment, hold or rejection) appends 3-8
   entries to [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) (brief L1): what happened, what it cost, the rule it implies, the playbook change.
2. **Versioned changes.** A rule change edits this file, adds a [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) entry and bumps
   `PLAYBOOK_VERSION` in `lib/cyrus/onboarding/types.ts` (major = a phase or gate changes; minor = a new template,
   checklist item or criterion; patch = wording). Records carry the `playbookVersion` they were brought up to.
3. **Docs coverage hook.** `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` fails when the version differs between code, this file and
   the changelog; when a template or brief this file links is missing; when the ladder table or gate list here drifts
   from the code; when LESSONS.md loses its shape; and when any game record claims more maturity than its evidence.
   (There is no repo-wide docs-coverage test on `feature/cyrus-r2` today; when r46's docs work adds one, this file
   should be registered in it.)
4. **Quarterly review** by the owner of the scorecard weights and threshold against the games actually onboarded.

# Cyrus game onboarding playbook

Playbook version: **1.0.0** (2026-10-11). Changelog: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Lessons: [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md).
Owner brief 2026-10-11: onboarding a new game must be flawless and repeatable, and this document keeps improving.
Minecraft is the reference implementation. Hytale and FiveM/RedM are ON HOLD and appear only as worked case studies
([CASE-STUDIES.md](CASE-STUDIES.md)).

This is a living document. It changes only through the loop in [How this playbook stays current](#how-this-playbook-stays-current).

## Start here

```
npx tsx scripts/cyrus/new-game.ts <gameId> --name "Game Name" [--language Lua] [--engine unity]
```
The scaffolder writes the skeleton (adapter at maturity `planned`, GameSupport stub, empty knowledge pack, eval-set
stub, onboarding record, checklist and doc stubs) and **registers nothing**: no adapter in `ADAPTERS`, no catalog row,
no flag. It is idempotent (an existing file is never overwritten). `--docs-only` writes only
`docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (use it for screening, before anyone writes code). `--manifest` prints the derived
capability manifest. Then work through `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` phase by phase.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/record.json` | phase, status, declared maturity, **evidence**, emitters, owner gate signatures, research reused |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/TODO.md` | the checklist (parsed by `lib/cyrus/onboarding/todo.ts`, shown on `/admin/cyrus/games`) |
| `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/*.md` | the filled templates: SCORECARD, RESEARCH, CAPABILITY, ADAPTER, ASSETS, LEGAL, VERIFICATION, LAUNCH |
| `lib/cyrus/onboarding/` | types (phases, gates, ladder), `health.ts` (ladder exit criteria + record checks), `manifest.ts` (derived capability manifest), `todo.ts`, `records.server.ts` |
| `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` | onboarding health over every record, docs coverage, scaffolder end to end |
| `templates/` | the templates the scaffolder copies, and `templates/agent-briefs/` |

## Principles (non-negotiable)
1. **Delivery first.** A game fits Cyrus only if what we build reaches players without each player installing it by
   hand, or the product is honest that it is a download (research H: "a delivery problem first").
2. **Evidence over claims.** A maturity, a pass rate, a "supported" exists only if it ran and is recorded with a date.
   The onboarding health test fails a record that claims more than its evidence.
3. **Reuse before research.** Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` and the case studies first. Never pay twice for
   the same page. Every record lists the research it reused.
4. **Honest unknowns.** Every fact is labelled V / V-s / U; an unknown stays in `GameSupport.unknowns` until verified.
5. **Game files never ship.** `redistributeBase: false` always; game-derived content is job-only and never enters a
   library; game binaries and decompiled code never enter git.
6. **Host seam.** New Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through `lib/cyrus/host` (`test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts`).
7. **Flag nothing on.** Registration, catalog status, settings and deploys are owner gates.
8. **One heavy job at a time** on node-2 through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost`; nothing heavy on the primary.

## Roles
| Role | Who | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | the owner only | signs the gates below; decides legal, money, flags, launch |
| Research agent | Sonnet, one pass per area | phases 0, 1, 5 (sources), 6 runs, 7 adversarial read |
| Build agent | Opus, few agents, one owner per file | phases 2, 3 (proposal), 4, 8 |
| Reviewer | a second agent | adversarial security pass, research spot-check of U labels |

Agent briefs with frugality and safety rules baked in: [templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md](templates/agent-briefs/COMMON-RULES.md),
[SCREENING](templates/agent-briefs/SCREENING.md), [RESEARCH](templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md) (R1-R9, one per area),
[BUILD](templates/agent-briefs/BUILD.md) (B1-B5), [REVIEW](templates/agent-briefs/REVIEW.md) (verification run,
adversarial pass, lessons learned).

## Owner gates
| Gate | Phase | The owner signs that |
|---|---|---|
| **G0-go** | 0 | the screening verdict is accepted (GO, or LATER / NO with the reason) |
| **G1-research** | 1 | the research report is accepted (unknowns listed, nothing invented) |
| **G3-tooling** | 3 | new apps, workers, licences and costs are approved |
| **G5-assets** | 5 | the asset sources and the licence ledger are approved |
| **G6-beta** | 6 | the maturity bump to beta is approved (evidence attached) |
| **G7-legal** | 7 | the EULA / mod policy / AI terms were read; `legal.reviewed` flips |
| **G8-flags** | 8 | the flag order and plan gating are approved |
| **G9-launch** | 9 | the game goes `live` in the catalog |

A gate is signed by writing `{ "by": "<owner>", "at": "<ISO date>" }` into `record.json` `gates` and ticking the
`OWNER GATE` line in `TODO.md`. Agents never sign. Games whose work predates this playbook carry `retrofit: true`:
missing early gates are warnings, never back-filled signatures.

```
 P0 screen --G0--> P1 research --G1--> P2 capability --> P3 tooling --G3--> P4 knowledge+build
      |                                                                        |
      +--> LATER / NO (status on-hold / rejected, holdReason)                  v
 P9 launch+upkeep <--G9-- P8 integration <--G8-- P7 legal <--G7-- P6 verify <--G6-- P5 assets <--G5--+
```
P5 can run in parallel with P3/P4 (different files, different agent). P7 legal facts are gathered from P0 on; the
owner's review closes it.

---

## Phase 0 Screening
**Purpose:** a cheap go / no-go before anyone researches deeply. **Budget:** one Sonnet pass, about 10 pages.
**Entry:** a game name. **Template:** [templates/SCREENING-SCORECARD.md](templates/SCREENING-SCORECARD.md).

| # | Criterion | Weight | Knockout |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delivery path to players | 20 | K1: manual client install only -> at most LATER |
| 2 | Mod policy / EULA / AI + commercial terms | 15 | K2: mods or paid mod services forbidden -> NO |
| 3 | Server availability + fit on Nxeon hosting | 15 | K3: no dedicated server -> NO for hosting |
| 4 | Formats and toolchain: licences + OS | 10 | |
| 5 | Asset-redistribution constraints | 10 | K4: a mod must contain game files -> NO |
| 6 | AI feasibility | 10 | |
| 7 | Audience / demand (sourced numbers only) | 15 | |
| 8 | Maintenance burden | 5 | |

Each criterion scores 0-5; total = sum(weight x score / 5), out of 100. **Recommended threshold: GO at 65+, LATER at
50-64, NO under 50**, knockouts override. Two or more U-labelled criteria of weight 15+ cap the verdict at LATER.
The verdict names the **narrowest viable first lane** (e.g. "server plugins only", "texture-only on user templates").

**Exit:** scorecard filled with labelled sources; verdict + first lane + revisit trigger; record status set
(`active`, or `on-hold` / `rejected` with `holdReason`). **Gate G0-go.**

## Phase 1 Deep research
**Purpose:** every fact the adapter needs, verified. **Template:** [templates/RESEARCH-REPORT.md](templates/RESEARCH-REPORT.md).
**Briefs:** R1-R9 in [templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md](templates/agent-briefs/RESEARCH.md) (bundle into three passes for small games).

Research areas (one section each in RESEARCH.md): languages and runtimes; mod loaders / APIs; asset formats (mesh,
texture, material, sound, animation, UI); animation / motion system; config conventions; networking; packaging and
install; update / outdated signals; version cadence; community norms; legal; verification lane.

Rules: official sources first (loader docs, source repos, LICENSE via the GitHub API, release feeds); host wikis are
secondary and labelled; a page that returns 403 is reported as such (Hytale's support pages did) and the claim stays
V-s; "not found" is a valid answer.

**Exit:** every RESEARCH.md section answered or explicitly unknown; contract gaps against the shared types listed;
ranked unknowns + owner decisions. **Gate G1-research.**

## Phase 2 Capability mapping
**Purpose:** turn research into the typed contract and decide what Cyrus can honestly offer.
**Templates:** [templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md](templates/CAPABILITY-WORKSHEET.md), [templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md](templates/ADAPTER-CHECKLIST.md). **Brief:** B1.

1. Fill `lib/cyrus/games/<id>.ts` (GameSupport: versions, install, verification, dangerous APIs, breakage risks,
   outdated signals, categories, sources, unknowns).
2. Fill `lib/cyrus/adapters/<id>.ts` (GameAdapter: artifacts with honest availability, toolchain, knowledge ref,
   versions, assetDelivery per kind, install, testLane, routeRules with honest limit messages). Maturity stays `planned`.
3. Fill the AssetProfile (formats, channel map, colour spaces, normal convention, max resolution, UV + skeleton policy,
   packaging, delivery strategy, worker class, required game files, legal with `reviewed: false`, validators, preview
   shader, catalog fit hints, motion capability). `validateAssetProfile()` must return no issues.
4. **Derive the capability manifest** (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/manifest.ts`, `new-game.ts <id> --manifest`): for each
   studio / tool (Texture, Sound, Model, Motion, Config, Data Pack studios; designers; creatures; library fit; import;
   Mod Packs + conflicts; Test Flight; install onto Nxeon servers; Server Doctor) the state **usable** (adapter supports
   it + a game emitter exists + its delivery / route is available), **planned** (something is missing, with the reason)
   or **hidden** (the game cannot use it; never shown to customers). Plus route availability, worker classes
   (linux-cpu / windows-tools / gpu), required game files (none / user-supplied / platform-licensed) and the **legal
   class per asset type** from the ledger (`lib/cyrus/assets3d/ledger.ts`; game-derived = job-only, never in a library).
5. List **contract gaps**: anything the shared types cannot express (see the cross-game list in CASE-STUDIES.md).
   Raise them; do not work around them silently.

**Exit:** files typed and validated; worksheet agrees with the derived manifest; contract gaps listed; health test green.

## Phase 3 Tooling decisions
**Purpose:** decide, per studio and artifact, what has to be brought in, before anyone builds it.

Decision tree (per studio / artifact in the worksheet):
```
Can an existing Cyrus studio produce it (the neutral core: textures as lossless channel layers, glTF + sidecar,
MotionSpec, ConfigSpec)?
 |- yes, and the game reads the format directly ............ EMITTER ONLY (a lowering/export in the adapter's lane)
 |- yes, but the game needs a different container/encoding .. EXPORTER + CONVERTER (pick a library, licence check)
 |- no: new language / compiler ............................ NEW TOOLCHAIN (build-host package, sandboxed compile)
 |- no: game-specific authoring tool ........................ NEW APP / WORKER (licence, OS, sandbox, cost) or HIDE
 '- no free / licensable tool exists ........................ HIDE the studio for this game (state = hidden)
```
**Licence check** (read the tool's own LICENSE, via the GitHub API when it is a repo):
| Licence | Rule |
|---|---|
| MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 / zlib | ok in workers and libraries |
| GPL / LGPL | run only as a **separate process** on user data; never link, embed or ship it (Blockbench, Sollumz) |
| none declared / "NOASSERTION" | legal review first (CodeWalker, Crowbar) |
| closed / proprietary EULA | no, unless the owner licenses it explicitly |
| community licence with region or use limits | no (Hunyuan3D excludes EU/UK/KR) |

**Sandbox + isolation:** every tool that touches user data runs as an unprivileged user with no network, a read-only
filesystem except a tmpfs work dir, CPU / memory / time caps and outputs re-validated by a Linux validator (pattern:
the meshgen Blender sandbox and Test Flight's loopback netns, research AC).

**Windows worker rules** (only when a Windows-only tool is unavoidable): ephemeral VM per job (or snapshot revert);
pull-based job queue; signed job manifest; allow-listed tools only; no outbound network except the broker; no Proxmox
or Nxeon credentials on the guest; hard timeout and caps; outputs returned through object storage and **re-scanned on
Linux**; a platform-licensed game install never lives on it without a separate legal review (`validateAssetProfile`
`windows_licensed`). The first game that needs it is the forcing function that proves the worker; no Windows fleet.

**Cost:** compute per build (node-2 minutes), storage per tenant, licence fees, model tokens per build (estimate,
labelled), owner time for real-client days.

**Exit:** every planned / hidden studio has a decision; every new tool has licence + sandbox + cost; the emitters
list in `record.json` names what will exist. **Gate G3-tooling.**

## Phase 4 Knowledge + build
**Purpose:** make the AI write correct mods for this game and prove it with tools, not opinions. **Briefs:** B2, B3.

- **API sheet:** verified facts, one per line, tagged `[Type] ...` so retrieval can inject only what a plan touches
  (pattern: `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts`; Minecraft uses `services/modbuilder/sheets/<version>.md`).
- **Failure rules:** `detect` regex + `fix` hint + `why` (+ `autofix` when a deterministic rewrite exists).
- **Dangerous API list:** block / warn patterns in GameSupport and in the scanner / validator; negative tests for each.
- **Compiler / validator toolchain:** pinned versions, runs on node-2 via devhost, against public loader packages;
  game binaries only in a node-2 cache. A pure-TS validator for languages without a compiler (Zomboid's Lua lint).
- **Scan rules:** what the generated code may reach (files, network, processes, reflection, native code); Minecraft's
  `services/modbuilder/scan.js` is the model (bytecode + source).
- **Test Flight equivalent:** how to boot the dedicated server headless (download method, image, RAM/CPU, ready line,
  install step, the mod's own load line, a console / RCON / REST channel for functional checks, clean stop). Design it
  here, run it in phase 6. Minecraft: `lib/cyrus/testflight` + `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight`.
- **Eval set:** `services/modbuilder/eval/games/<id>.jsonl` with **at least 40 prompts**: 30 across the game's
  categories (simple / standard / complex) + 10 adversarial that must be refused (network, file deletion, admin abuse,
  cheats, obfuscation). No `todo` rows left. (Minecraft's lives in `services/modbuilder/eval/prompts.jsonl` + `sets/`;
  the per-game folder keeps new games out of the Minecraft loaders.)

**Exit:** template or real build output passes the validator (`evidence.templateValidated`); eval set complete;
Test Flight equivalent designed with its recipe in VERIFICATION.md.

## Phase 5 Assets for the library
**Purpose:** give the game's studios and builds a licence-clean starting library. **Template:** [templates/ASSET-SOURCING.md](templates/ASSET-SOURCING.md). **Brief:** R9.

- **Reuse first.** The shared library already holds ~61k CC0 / CC-BY items (10.3k models, 2.9k PBR sets, 1.4k HDRIs,
  38k sprites, 4.2k icons, 3.1k sounds; research J) plus ~2k motion items (research S). Run the per-game fit
  (`lib/cyrus/library/v2/fit.ts`, driven by `assetProfile.catalog`) before fetching anything new.
- **CC0 only by default.** CC-BY only after the owner's attribution decision (still open). Read every licence on the
  source's own page and quote it; never trust an aggregator label (Papyszoo's blanket "CC0" was wrong in places);
  watch for licence changes (Quaternius moved new packs to a no-redistribution licence on 2026-08-28).
- **Where to look by game type:** voxel / pixel games: Kenney 2D, game-icons, pixel packs, procedural (Texture Studio);
  stylised 3D: Quaternius, KayKit, Kenney 3D, Base Mesh; realistic 3D: Poly Haven, ambientCG, Smithsonian CC0 scans;
  sound: Kenney audio, BrainBytes / Ben Burnes, OpenGameArt CC0, FSD50K CC0 clips; motion: KayKit + Quaternius
  animation libraries, OGA CC0 flipbooks. Rejected sources stay rejected (Freesound scraping, Mixamo, Sonniss, ...;
  research J / S ledgers).
- **Game-derived content never public.** Base meshes, textures and sounds of the game are `game-derived`: job
  retention, never stored beyond the job, never in any library, never redistributed; a retexture ships the delta.
  **BYO-assets flow:** the user supplies their own template / base file with an ownership attestation
  (`attestationRequired`), Cyrus works on it inside the job, the deliverable carries only user content.
- **Ledger:** every staged item has a source / pack / licence / quote / url / retrieved row (`LICENCE-LEDGER.csv`).
- **Catalog fit fields:** `accepts` per kind (native / convert / none), `noneReasons`, `styleAffinity`, `triBudget`,
  `textureRes`, `audio` (format, channels, max seconds).
- **Ingestion with the existing scripts:** stage under `/tank/cyrus-library-staging/` (never git, never prod);
  measure with `scripts/cyrus/catalog-stage-a.ts --cc0-only`; import into the node-2 throwaway DB with
  `scripts/cyrus/library-import.ts --dry-run`, then `--pg --twice` (idempotency).

**Exit:** ASSETS.md filled; ledger rows for every new source; fit sample checked. **Gate G5-assets.**

## Phase 6 Verification
**Purpose:** measured evidence for the maturity claim. **Template:** [templates/VERIFICATION-PLAN.md](templates/VERIFICATION-PLAN.md). **Brief:** V1.

- **Flight tests:** headless boot + load line + functional checks + clean stop, on real server software in a node-2
  sandbox (loopback only, own netns, random secrets). A skipped required check is not a pass.
- **Real-client day:** a human with a real client joins and sees each archetype work (client-side features cannot be
  verified headless). Name the tester and the day.
- **Pass-rate evidence:** measured only, recorded in `record.json` `evidence` with ref + date + passed / total; no rate
  shown under 10 samples (`lib/cyrus/eval/passrate.ts` MIN_PUBLISH_N).

### Maturity ladder
The exit criteria are code (`lib/cyrus/onboarding/health.ts` LADDER_CRITERIA); the test checks this table matches.

| Rung | Exact exit criteria |
|---|---|
| planned | Nothing built. Adapter file + GameSupport stub + record exist; every unknown is listed. |
| template | Canned / template output exists and passes the game's validator. |
| beta | Real AI build path: compile >= 90% over >= 20 builds, the safety scan runs on every build, eval run >= 20 measured prompts at >= 80%; owner gate G6-beta signed. |
| stable | Beta plus headless boot + functional flights >= 95% over >= 10 flights, one real-client day, legal reviewed by the owner (G7-legal) and a no-manual delivery path. |

The adapter's `maturity` may never exceed the record's `declaredMaturity`, which may never exceed what the evidence
proves. **Exit:** evidence recorded; maturity bump proposed. **Gate G6-beta** (for beta).

## Phase 7 Legal + security review
**Template:** [templates/LEGAL-CHECKLIST.md](templates/LEGAL-CHECKLIST.md). **Briefs:** R7 (facts), S1 (adversarial pass).

Legal: EULA / ToS read in full; mod policy; AI-content terms and mod-site disclosure rules; redistribution (never base
files); hosting terms (provider programmes, licence keys, server caps: Hytale's Game Server Provider entitlement is the
example); monetisation; trademark. `commercialOk` / `aiOk` stay "unknown" until a reviewer read the source.
Security: threat model delta for the new language / runtime / tools / delivery path; dangerous-API tests; sandbox
review; Windows worker review if any; second-agent adversarial pass with VERIFIED-TEST / RUN / READ labels (research AC).

**Exit:** checklist complete, findings fixed or listed. **Gate G7-legal** (the owner flips `legal.reviewed`).

## Phase 8 Nxeon integration
**Brief:** B5. Every item behind a flag that defaults OFF. Touchpoints for a new game:

| Touchpoint | File(s) |
|---|---|
| Cyrus game registry (studio ring, version picker, marketing copy) | `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (stays `soon`), `lib/cyrus/data.ts` GAMES (logo from the owner's art under `public/cyrus/games/`) |
| Admin status override + "can be live" rule | `lib/cyrus/game-status.ts` (`CYRUS_BUILDABLE_GAMES` only with a real build pipeline) |
| Adapter registration (router, retexture export targets) | `lib/cyrus/adapters/index.ts` + the count in `test/cyrus-engine-core.test.ts`; `lib/cyrus/modelstudio/retex/export.ts` iterates ADAPTERS |
| Template generator (previews) | `lib/cyrus/engine/games/<id>.ts` |
| Categories | `lib/cyrus/categories.ts` |
| Nxeon game family + installer | `lib/games.ts` GAME_FAMILIES (the slug can differ: `projectzomboid` vs Cyrus `zomboid`), `lib/mods/installers/<game>.ts`, `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, `worker/game-mods.ts` |
| Install paths, grants and scopes | server grants (`servers.read`, `inventory.read`, `files.write.mods`, `server.restart`, `logs.read.tail`, `pack.set`) via the host seam; paths regex-pinned |
| Delivery strategy | `lib/cyrus/delivery` (journal, rollback, health) for server-side installs; workshop / download flows are guidance, never auto-publish |
| Plan gating | `lib/cyrus/engine-core/asset-gate.ts` (studios per plan), `lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts` |
| Readiness + onboarding on admin | `docs/cyrus/readiness/<id>.md`, `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/` (both shown on `/admin/cyrus/games`) |
| Marketing "coming soon" -> live | customer-facing copy only, no invented stats; What's New only for customer-facing changes |

**Exit:** all touchpoints wired behind flags, adapter registered, flag order written. **Gate G8-flags.**

## Phase 9 Launch + upkeep
**Template:** [templates/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md](templates/LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md).
Launch: maturity >= beta, health test green, gates G0-G8 signed, a real install on a Nxeon server of the game (owner /
test account) with restart, verify, uninstall and rollback, support macros drafted (never sent without approval),
docs/DOCUMENTATION.md updated, then the owner flips the catalog status. **Gate G9-launch.**
Deploys only through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` then `scripts/promote-production.sh` (owner / root).

Upkeep: patch watch (source + cadence + who), outdated signals wired to the lifecycle (`GameSupport.outdatedSignals`),
version-table bump procedure (registry + knowledge pack + failure rules + harness re-run), quarterly policy re-read
(`legal.retrievedAt`), monthly eval regression (budget-gated), support macros kept current.

**Exit (and the end of every onboarding, including abandoned ones):** lessons learned appended to LESSONS.md.

---

## Frugality rules
- One Sonnet pass per research area at about 10 pages; bundle areas for small games (three passes, not nine).
- Opus only for phase 2 / 4 / 8 build work; one owner per file; at most two agents at once per game.
- Reuse the case studies and the cross-game contract gap list; extend them, do not rewrite them.
- No paid model calls (eval runs, image / 3D APIs) without the owner's budget in the brief.
- Templates are cheap to fill on purpose: tables over prose, labels over paragraphs.

## How this playbook stays current
1. **Lessons learned after every onboarding.** The phase 9 exit (and any abandonment, hold or rejection) appends 3-8
   entries to [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) (brief L1): what happened, what it cost, the rule it implies, the playbook change.
2. **Versioned changes.** A rule change edits this file, adds a [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) entry and bumps
   `PLAYBOOK_VERSION` in `lib/cyrus/onboarding/types.ts` (major = a phase or gate changes; minor = a new template,
   checklist item or criterion; patch = wording). Records carry the `playbookVersion` they were brought up to.

# Onboarding lessons learned

Appended after every onboarding (phase 9 exit) and whenever an onboarding is put on hold, rejected or abandoned
(brief L1 in templates/agent-briefs/REVIEW.md). Format per entry, newest last:

```
### L<n> <short title> (<game>, <date>)
What happened. What it cost.
Rule: the rule it implies.
Playbook change: the section that changed (+ version), or "none".
```

The first entries are retro-fitted from the work that predates the playbook (research files in
`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` and the game readiness checklists).

### L1 Delivery decides the product, not the editor (multi-game research, 2026-10-10)
Research H found most "3D support" requests fail on delivery: Valheim, Rust and Fallout cannot push assets to players,
so a texture studio for them would build things nobody can use.
Rule: delivery path is criterion 1 (weight 20) and a knockout for manual-install-only games.
Playbook change: phase 0 scorecard (1.0.0).

### L2 Template previews are not a build path (Terraria / Valheim / Zomboid, 2026-10-08)
Three games got verified GameSupport files, generators and validators, but every output is template code and the
build service only builds Minecraft; their readiness lists "real AI generation path" as must-have item 1.
Rule: maturity `template` is a real rung with its own exit criteria; beta needs the real AI build path with measured
compile and eval rates.
Playbook change: maturity ladder (1.0.0).

### L3 Official pages can be unreachable; label it (Hytale, 2026-10-10)
Hytale's support pages returned 403, so the server-provider terms rest on host wikis (V-s); the AI-asset terms are
still unknown and are the main legal blocker.
Rule: a 403 is reported, the claim stays V-s, and the unknown blocks legal review, not the research report.
Playbook change: phase 1 rules (1.0.0).

### L4 Aggregator licence labels lie (asset ingest, 2026-10-10)
A blanket "CC0" aggregator held Sonniss GDC and unlabelled packs; Quaternius moved new packs to a no-redistribution
licence on 2026-08-28.
Rule: read every licence on the source's own page; pin and quote; re-check sources before each ingest.
Playbook change: phase 5 (1.0.0).

### L5 Ids differ between Cyrus and Nxeon (Zomboid, 2026-10-11)
Cyrus calls it `zomboid`; the Nxeon game family is `projectzomboid` (lib/games.ts). Any join between Cyrus records and
Nxeon servers needs an explicit mapping.
Rule: phase 8 records the Nxeon family slug next to the Cyrus id.
Playbook change: phase 8 touchpoint table (1.0.0).

### L6 Adapter data lags the code (Minecraft, 2026-10-11)
The Minecraft adapter still declares texture / sound / model delivery and `testLane.boot` as "planned" while pack
hosting, the studios and Test Flight exist behind flags. Honest for customers (flags are off), but it means the derived
manifest shows Texture Studio as planned for the reference game.
Rule: flipping a delivery flag on is incomplete until the adapter's availability flips with it (launch checklist).
Playbook change: none yet (tracked in IMPROVEMENTS.md).
