# Onboarding case studies (retro-fit, playbook 1.0.0)

How the games Cyrus already touched map onto [PLAYBOOK.md](PLAYBOOK.md), and the exact gaps each would hit next.
Written 2026-10-11 by r47 from existing research only (nothing re-fetched): research files in
`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/` (H-3d-games, N-hytale, R-motion-effects, J / S asset ingest, AC security) and the
readiness checklists in `docs/cyrus/readiness/`. Labels from the sources carry over (V / V-s / U). Scorecard numbers
below are **r47's judgement applied to that research, not measurements**; they show how the rubric behaves.
Records: `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/record.json` + `TODO.md`.

## Retro scorecard (weights: delivery 20, policy 15, server fit 15, toolchain 10, redistribution 10, AI 10, audience 15, upkeep 5)

| Game | Deliv. | Policy | Server | Tools | Redist. | AI | Audience | Upkeep | Total | Knockouts | Verdict (rubric) | Status today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minecraft (Paper plugins) | 5 | 3 (EULA parked) | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 3 | **90** | none | GO | reference, beta |
| Terraria (TShock lane) | 4 | 3 (U) | 5 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 4 | **77** | none | GO (TShock first) | template, phase 4 |
| Valheim | 1 | 3 | 5 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 3 | **63** | K1 (every client installs) | LATER | template, phase 4 |
| Project Zomboid | 2 | 2 (no selling access) | 5 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 2 | **63** | none hard; delivery weak | LATER | template, phase 4 |
| Hytale | 5 | 3 (AI U) | 3 (GSP entitlement) | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 (U) | 1 (EA weekly) | **77** | none; 2 U criteria >= 15 cap it | LATER until verified | on hold |
| FiveM / RedM | 5 | 1 (tolerated, revocable) | 4 | 1 (Windows, no-licence tools) | 2 | 3 | 5 | 3 | **66** | none hard; legal is the risk | GO only texture-only, after legal | on hold |

Totals: sum(weight x score / 5). The rubric reproduces the research verdicts: Minecraft and Terraria GO, Valheim and
Zomboid LATER on delivery, Hytale held back by unverified policy / hosting terms, FiveM narrow and legal-gated.

---

## Minecraft (reference implementation)
- **Phases done:** 0-5 in substance (research E, A, A2, B, C, D, R, J, S), P6 partly (real Test Flight runs: 4 versions
  flown in `matrix-r35-flights-2026-10-11.json`), P7 security (AC, no HIGH finding), P8 partly (adapter registered,
  grants and delivery behind flags).
- **Evidence:** real AI build path (javac + `scan.js` on every build), v6 harness 28/28 built and 13/13 loaded, 4/4
  flights. Proven rung: **beta**. Not stable: flights under the 10 floor, no real-client day, Mojang EULA parked.
- **Gaps:** legal review parked by the owner; the adapter declares pack delivery and boot as "planned" while the code
  exists behind flags (lesson L6), so the derived manifest shows Texture / Sound / Model Studio and Data Pack Studio as
  planned; paid eval baseline owner-gated; 26.x lane needs Java 25 on the build VM.
- **Use it as the pattern for:** adapter shape, version registry with pinned server builds + hashes, knowledge as
  version sheets, scanner (bytecode + source), Test Flight (loopback Paper, RCON checks), eval set + pass-rate page.

## Terraria (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport with two flavours (TShock server plugins C# .NET 9; tModLoader content mods .NET 8),
  knowledge pack, template generator, validator, compile harness on node-2 (78/78 template mods compiled), Nxeon already
  installs TShock plugins (`worker/game-mods.ts`, rollback on a missing "Plugin X initiated" line).
- **Maps to:** P0-P1 done (readiness doc), P2 half (GameSupport yes, **no adapter file, no AssetProfile**), P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + capability manifest; (2) build-service C# lane (`dotnet build` in a sandbox, NuGet
  cache, no network after restore); (3) load test (TShock Docker `ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock`, the "initiated" log line);
  (4) **2D asset profile**: tModLoader sprites are PNG sheets with frame animation, not Minecraft's pixel items: the
  Texture Studio needs a sprite-sheet exporter and the motion core a flipbook lowering; (5) eval set (40); (6) tModLoader
  is a second product on a different game version (1.4.4.9 vs TShock 1.4.5.8) and Nxeon has no tModLoader server.
- **New apps:** .NET 8 + .NET 9 SDKs on the build host (Linux, MIT); tModLoader for `.tmod` packaging (MIT).

## Valheim (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport, knowledge pack (~28 API facts, 11 failure rules), generator, validator, compile harness
  against the 1.0.17 dedicated-server assemblies (downloaded anonymously into a node-2 cache, never committed).
- **Maps to:** P0 would say **LATER** (K1: every player needs the same mods via r2modman); P2 half; P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + manifest; (2) delivery: `side: both` mods need a player download flow (r2modman profile
  code), so Install onto Nxeon servers is usable only for server-only archetypes; (3) **assets need Unity AssetBundles
  built with the matching Unity 6 editor**: a new app, licence unchecked, Windows / heavy, so Texture / Model / Sound
  Studio stay hidden; (4) load test (`lloesche/valheim-server` with `BEPINEX=true`, grep `LogOutput.log`); (5)
  Thunderstore rejects "untested or non-functional AI-generated mods" (publish only after load test, never auto); (6)
  owner decision on downloading public server DLLs at build time.
- **New apps:** .NET SDK, BepInEx publicizer (MIT), Unity 6 editor (licence + OS review), r2modman (player side).

## Project Zomboid (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport for Build 42 (17 dangerous-API rules), knowledge pack (14 API lines, 12 failure rules),
  generator, a pure-TS Lua 5.1 lexer / structure validator.
- **Maps to:** P0 **LATER** on delivery (Workshop upload needs the creator's own Steam account; otherwise manual);
  policy forbids selling access to mods (the store must keep them free); P2 half; P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + manifest; (2) no Lua runtime for unit tests (lua5.1 + busted or wasmoon / fengari: an
  owner dependency decision); (3) load test (SteamCMD anonymous app 380870 in a throwaway container, 4-6 GB RAM, grep
  `console.txt`); (4) assets: PNG icons / clothing textures could reuse the Texture Studio with an exporter, `.fbx`
  models need a converter (none on the box), sounds `.ogg` via script definitions; (5) id mapping `zomboid` ->
  Nxeon family `projectzomboid`; (6) install guard: only `b42` servers.
- **New apps:** Lua 5.1 runtime + busted (or a JS Lua VM), FBX -> glTF converter (only if models are in scope).

## Hytale (ON HOLD: summary of N-hytale.md)
- **Verdict:** CONDITIONAL GO, adapter at maturity planned / template, not beta. Blockers are not technical:
  (a) customer hosting needs Hytale's **Game Server Provider entitlement** (`sessions.unlimited_servers`; without it
  100 servers per licence and per-server OAuth device auth), (b) **AI-asset terms unread** (support pages 403), (c)
  early-access formats change weekly.
- **Facts that hold (V):** server-streamed asset packs (players install nothing); `.blockymodel` (cuboids + quads only,
  fixed materials) + PNG at 32 px/unit (blocks) / 64 px/unit (characters); Java 25 plugins with Gradle from
  maven.hytale.com, `manifest.json` with `IncludesAssetPack`; EULA lets creators own and even monetise mods if no game
  files are included; UDP 5520 (QUIC), 4-8 GB RAM.
- **Exact gaps on the playbook:** P1: `.blockymodel` / `.blockyanim` schemas not published (derive from a real file /
  the Blockbench plugin source); max texture size, node limits, hot reload unknown. P2: needs a **new emitter**
  (RigSpec -> `.blockymodel`) and a **new animation lowering** (`.blockyanim` keyframes); the draft AssetProfile in
  N-hytale.md is ready to paste. P3: Java 25 toolchain (already planned for Minecraft 26.x); Blockbench (GPL) only as
  optional, never embedded. P4 / P6: **Test Flight needs per-server OAuth** (a credentialed lane: new contract need).
  P7: GSP terms + AI terms. P8: no Hytale SKU on Nxeon (heavier than Minecraft).

## FiveM / RedM (ON HOLD: summary of H-3d-games.md + R-motion-effects.md)
- **Verdict:** START texture-only on user-supplied templates (liveries, clothing, props), server-streamed via the
  resource's `stream/` folder; NO new meshes, maps or missions (Take-Two excludes them); no monetisation features
  (Tebex is the only authorised partner). Motion: pick from existing animation dictionaries + ptfx presets only; NO
  authoring new `.ycd`.
- **Exact gaps on the playbook:** P0: policy scores 1 (tolerance, revocable, not a licence). P2: GameSupport has no
  **JavaScript** language and no multi-language resource (Lua 5.4 / C# / JS); routes need a "resource" with a
  `stream/` folder, which `ARTIFACT_ROUTES` cannot express. P3: **YTD packing needs the Windows worker** (CodeWalker:
  no licence declared -> legal review; DirectXTex `texconv` MIT is fine; Sollumz GPL-3 only as a separate process).
  P5: game-derived base textures are BYO-only (user template, attestation, delta shipped). P6: FXServer boot needs a
  Cfx.re licence key (U): another credentialed Test Flight lane. P7: Take-Two + Cfx.re terms are the whole risk.

---

## Studios and tools needed per game

| | Minecraft | Terraria | Valheim | Zomboid | Hytale (hold) | FiveM / RedM (hold) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Texture | pixel PNG 16-64 px, Texture Studio (have) | 2D sprite sheets: sprite exporter (new, tML only) | Unity AssetBundle: hidden until Unity lane | PNG icons / clothing: exporter (new) | PNG 32/64 px per unit: pixel studio reuse + exporter | YTD (DDS in RSC) on user templates: Windows worker |
| Sound | mono Ogg Vorbis in pack (have) | tML sounds (format U) | Unity AudioClip in bundle: hidden | `.ogg` + script sound defs: exporter (new) | format U | `.awc` banks (U): hidden |
| Model / animation | bbmodel / item model JSON + BetterModel (have) | none (2D): hidden | Unity prefabs: hidden | `.fbx` / `.X`: converter needed, hidden for now | `.blockymodel` + `.blockyanim`: new emitter + lowering | YDR/YFT: hidden (no new meshes) |
| Motion | display entities + BetterModel lowering (have) | flipbook lowering (new) | none | AnimSets (U): none | blockyanim lowering (new) | existing anim dicts + ptfx presets (pick only) |
| Config | `config.yml` (Config Studio, have) | TShock JSON / tML ModConfig (new emitter) | BepInEx `.cfg` (new emitter) | sandbox options (new emitter) | JSON assets (U) | `server.cfg` convars + `fxmanifest.lua` (new) |
| Designers | Java emitters (have) | C# emitters (new) | C# Harmony (template only) | Lua (template only) | Java 25 plugin emitters (new API) | Lua / C# / JS resources (new) |
| Test Flight type | headless Paper + RCON on node-2 (have) | TShock Docker, log line + console (designed) | valheim-server Docker + BepInEx log (designed) | SteamCMD anon container + console.txt (designed) | Java 25 server + **per-server OAuth** (credentialed) | FXServer + **licence key** (credentialed, U) |
| Languages / runtimes | Java 21 / 25, JSON, mcfunction | C# .NET 9 (TShock), .NET 8 (tML) | C# (BepInEx 5, Harmony) | Lua 5.1 (Kahlua), PZ scripts, JSON | Java 25, JSON | Lua 5.4, C#, **JavaScript** |
| Extra apps | none beyond JDKs + Paper jars | .NET SDKs, tModLoader packer | .NET SDK, publicizer, **Unity 6 editor** | Lua 5.1 + busted, FBX converter | hytale-downloader, GSP account | **Windows worker**, texconv, CodeWalker (legal) |
| Worker class | linux-cpu | linux-cpu | linux-cpu (+ Unity: heavy, OS U) | linux-cpu | linux-cpu | **windows-tools** |
| Required game files | none | none (public NuGet) | server DLLs at build time (owner decision) | none | none (Assets.zip never shipped) | **user-supplied** templates |

## Cross-game contract gaps (raise before building game #2)
1. `GameSupport.language` has no **JavaScript** and no multi-language / runtime-version form (FiveM; Java 21 vs 25).
2. `ARTIFACT_ROUTES` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod) is Minecraft-shaped: no "asset pack + plugin"
   (Hytale), "stream resource" (FiveM), "content mod both sides" (tModLoader), "workshop item" (Zomboid, GMod).
3. `ASSET_KINDS` has no **animation** or **material**; the AssetProfile has no sound or UI format field (only the
   catalog `audio` hint).
4. Two delivery vocabularies: `AssetDelivery.via` (server-pushed-pack / client-zip / client-mod / server-files) vs
   `AssetProfile.delivery` (server-streamed / workshop-* / client-manual). Unify them.
5. `TestLane` cannot say "needs a credential" (Hytale OAuth per server, FiveM licence key): add a credentialed lane
   flag so the owner gate is explicit.
6. `InstallRules.side` is single-valued; Valheim and tModLoader decide side per archetype.
7. Knowledge lives in two systems (Minecraft version sheets vs GameSupport knowledge packs; research G-gaps (b)).
8. The template generators (`lib/cyrus/engine/games/*`) are not referenced from the adapter; the adapter should
   name its generator / build lane.
9. The Cyrus game id and the Nxeon game family slug can differ (`zomboid` / `projectzomboid`): one mapping table.

## Minecraft (reference implementation)
- **Phases done:** 0-5 in substance (research E, A, A2, B, C, D, R, J, S), P6 partly (real Test Flight runs: 4 versions
  flown in `matrix-r35-flights-2026-10-11.json`), P7 security (AC, no HIGH finding), P8 partly (adapter registered,
  grants and delivery behind flags).
- **Evidence:** real AI build path (javac + `scan.js` on every build), v6 harness 28/28 built and 13/13 loaded, 4/4
  flights. Proven rung: **beta**. Not stable: flights under the 10 floor, no real-client day, Mojang EULA parked.

  exists behind flags (lesson L6), so the derived manifest shows Texture / Sound / Model Studio and Data Pack Studio as
  planned; paid eval baseline owner-gated; 26.x lane needs Java 25 on the build VM.
- **Use it as the pattern for:** adapter shape, version registry with pinned server builds + hashes, knowledge as
  version sheets, scanner (bytecode + source), Test Flight (loopback Paper, RCON checks), eval set + pass-rate page.

## Terraria (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport with two flavours (TShock server plugins C# .NET 9; tModLoader content mods .NET 8),
  knowledge pack, template generator, validator, compile harness on node-2 (78/78 template mods compiled), Nxeon already
  installs TShock plugins (`worker/game-mods.ts`, rollback on a missing "Plugin X initiated" line).
- **Maps to:** P0-P1 done (readiness doc), P2 half (GameSupport yes, **no adapter file, no AssetProfile**), P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + capability manifest; (2) build-service C# lane (`dotnet build` in a sandbox, NuGet
  cache, no network after restore); (3) load test (TShock Docker `ghcr.io/pryaxis/tshock`, the "initiated" log line);
  (4) **2D asset profile**: tModLoader sprites are PNG sheets with frame animation, not Minecraft's pixel items: the
  Texture Studio needs a sprite-sheet exporter and the motion core a flipbook lowering; (5) eval set (40); (6) tModLoader
  is a second product on a different game version (1.4.4.9 vs TShock 1.4.5.8) and Nxeon has no tModLoader server.
- **New apps:** .NET 8 + .NET 9 SDKs on the build host (Linux, MIT); tModLoader for `.tmod` packaging (MIT).

## Valheim (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport, knowledge pack (~28 API facts, 11 failure rules), generator, validator, compile harness
  against the 1.0.17 dedicated-server assemblies (downloaded anonymously into a node-2 cache, never committed).
- **Maps to:** P0 would say **LATER** (K1: every player needs the same mods via r2modman); P2 half; P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + manifest; (2) delivery: `side: both` mods need a player download flow (r2modman profile
  code), so Install onto Nxeon servers is usable only for server-only archetypes; (3) **assets need Unity AssetBundles
  built with the matching Unity 6 editor**: a new app, licence unchecked, Windows / heavy, so Texture / Model / Sound
  Studio stay hidden; (4) load test (`lloesche/valheim-server` with `BEPINEX=true`, grep `LogOutput.log`); (5)
  Thunderstore rejects "untested or non-functional AI-generated mods" (publish only after load test, never auto); (6)
  owner decision on downloading public server DLLs at build time.
- **New apps:** .NET SDK, BepInEx publicizer (MIT), Unity 6 editor (licence + OS review), r2modman (player side).

## Project Zomboid (retro-fit, phase 4)
- **What exists:** GameSupport for Build 42 (17 dangerous-API rules), knowledge pack (14 API lines, 12 failure rules),
  generator, a pure-TS Lua 5.1 lexer / structure validator.
- **Maps to:** P0 **LATER** on delivery (Workshop upload needs the creator's own Steam account; otherwise manual);
  policy forbids selling access to mods (the store must keep them free); P2 half; P4 mostly.
- **Exact gaps:** (1) adapter + manifest; (2) no Lua runtime for unit tests (lua5.1 + busted or wasmoon / fengari: an
  owner dependency decision); (3) load test (SteamCMD anonymous app 380870 in a throwaway container, 4-6 GB RAM, grep
  `console.txt`); (4) assets: PNG icons / clothing textures could reuse the Texture Studio with an exporter, `.fbx`
  models need a converter (none on the box), sounds `.ogg` via script definitions; (5) id mapping `zomboid` ->
  Nxeon family `projectzomboid`; (6) install guard: only `b42` servers.
- **New apps:** Lua 5.1 runtime + busted (or a JS Lua VM), FBX -> glTF converter (only if models are in scope).

## Hytale (ON HOLD: summary of N-hytale.md)
- **Verdict:** CONDITIONAL GO, adapter at maturity planned / template, not beta. Blockers are not technical:
  (a) customer hosting needs Hytale's **Game Server Provider entitlement** (`sessions.unlimited_servers`; without it
  100 servers per licence and per-server OAuth device auth), (b) **AI-asset terms unread** (support pages 403), (c)
  early-access formats change weekly.
- **Facts that hold (V):** server-streamed asset packs (players install nothing); `.blockymodel` (cuboids + quads only,
  fixed materials) + PNG at 32 px/unit (blocks) / 64 px/unit (characters); Java 25 plugins with Gradle from
  maven.hytale.com, `manifest.json` with `IncludesAssetPack`; EULA lets creators own and even monetise mods if no game
  files are included; UDP 5520 (QUIC), 4-8 GB RAM.
- **Exact gaps on the playbook:** P1: `.blockymodel` / `.blockyanim` schemas not published (derive from a real file /
  the Blockbench plugin source); max texture size, node limits, hot reload unknown. P2: needs a **new emitter**
  (RigSpec -> `.blockymodel`) and a **new animation lowering** (`.blockyanim` keyframes); the draft AssetProfile in
  N-hytale.md is ready to paste. P3: Java 25 toolchain (already planned for Minecraft 26.x); Blockbench (GPL) only as
  optional, never embedded. P4 / P6: **Test Flight needs per-server OAuth** (a credentialed lane: new contract need).
  P7: GSP terms + AI terms. P8: no Hytale SKU on Nxeon (heavier than Minecraft).

## FiveM / RedM (ON HOLD: summary of H-3d-games.md + R-motion-effects.md)
- **Verdict:** START texture-only on user-supplied templates (liveries, clothing, props), server-streamed via the
  resource's `stream/` folder; NO new meshes, maps or missions (Take-Two excludes them); no monetisation features
  (Tebex is the only authorised partner). Motion: pick from existing animation dictionaries + ptfx presets only; NO
  authoring new `.ycd`.
- **Exact gaps on the playbook:** P0: policy scores 1 (tolerance, revocable, not a licence). P2: GameSupport has no
  **JavaScript** language and no multi-language resource (Lua 5.4 / C# / JS); routes need a "resource" with a
  `stream/` folder, which `ARTIFACT_ROUTES` cannot express. P3: **YTD packing needs the Windows worker** (CodeWalker:
  no licence declared -> legal review; DirectXTex `texconv` MIT is fine; Sollumz GPL-3 only as a separate process).
  P5: game-derived base textures are BYO-only (user template, attestation, delta shipped). P6: FXServer boot needs a
  Cfx.re licence key (U): another credentialed Test Flight lane. P7: Take-Two + Cfx.re terms are the whole risk.

| Designers | Java emitters (have) | C# emitters (new) | C# Harmony (template only) | Lua (template only) | Java 25 plugin emitters (new API) | Lua / C# / JS resources (new) |
| Test Flight type | headless Paper + RCON on node-2 (have) | TShock Docker, log line + console (designed) | valheim-server Docker + BepInEx log (designed) | SteamCMD anon container + console.txt (designed) | Java 25 server + **per-server OAuth** (credentialed) | FXServer + **licence key** (credentialed, U) |

## Cross-game contract gaps (raise before building game #2)
1. `GameSupport.language` has no **JavaScript** and no multi-language / runtime-version form (FiveM; Java 21 vs 25).
2. `ARTIFACT_ROUTES` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod) is Minecraft-shaped: no "asset pack + plugin"
   (Hytale), "stream resource" (FiveM), "content mod both sides" (tModLoader), "workshop item" (Zomboid, GMod).
3. `ASSET_KINDS` has no **animation** or **material**; the AssetProfile has no sound or UI format field (only the
   catalog `audio` hint).
4. Two delivery vocabularies: `AssetDelivery.via` (server-pushed-pack / client-zip / client-mod / server-files) vs
   `AssetProfile.delivery` (server-streamed / workshop-* / client-manual). Unify them.
5. `TestLane` cannot say "needs a credential" (Hytale OAuth per server, FiveM licence key): add a credentialed lane
   flag so the owner gate is explicit.
6. `InstallRules.side` is single-valued; Valheim and tModLoader decide side per archetype.
7. Knowledge lives in two systems (Minecraft version sheets vs GameSupport knowledge packs; research G-gaps (b)).
8. The template generators (`lib/cyrus/engine/games/*`) are not referenced from the adapter; the adapter should
   name its generator / build lane.
9. The Cyrus game id and the Nxeon game family slug can differ (`zomboid` / `projectzomboid`): one mapping table.

## Cyrus game onboarding kit (r47, branch `feature/cyrus-r47-onboarding`, NOT deployed, nothing switched on)

The repeatable way to bring a new game into Cyrus: `docs/cyrus/onboarding/` (start at `README.md` / `PLAYBOOK.md`). Ten phases (0 screening with a weighted go/no-go scorecard, 1 deep research, 2 capability mapping, 3 tooling decisions, 4 knowledge + build, 5 assets for the library, 6 verification, 7 legal + security, 8 Nxeon integration, 9 launch + upkeep), each with entry/exit criteria, and eight owner gates (G0-go ... G9-launch) that only the owner signs in `docs/cyrus/onboarding/games/<id>/record.json`.

**Code (pure, host-seam clean).** `lib/cyrus/onboarding/`: `types.ts` (phases, gates, `PLAYBOOK_VERSION`, the record type), `health.ts` (maturity ladder exit criteria as code: planned -> template -> beta -> stable; `checkRecord` fails a record or adapter that claims more than its recorded evidence), `manifest.ts` (derived capability manifest: per studio usable / planned / hidden with the reason, routes, worker classes, required game files, legal class per asset kind from the 3D ledger), `todo.ts` (checklist parser), `records.server.ts` (reads the records).

**Scaffolder.** `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/new-game.ts <gameId> --name "Name" [--language L] [--engine E] [--docs-only] [--dry-run]` writes the adapter at maturity `planned` (with a draft AssetProfile, `legal.reviewed: false`), a GameSupport stub with its unknowns, an empty knowledge pack, an eval-set stub (`services/modbuilder/eval/games/<id>.jsonl`, 30 + 10 adversarial `todo` slots, outside the Minecraft loaders' `sets/` glob), the record, the checklist and the doc stubs. Idempotent (never overwrites); registers nothing (no `ADAPTERS` entry, no catalog row, no setting). `--manifest` prints the derived manifest.

**Admin.** `/admin/cyrus/games` gains a read-only "Game onboarding" section (phase, status, declared vs proven maturity, checklist progress, open owner gates, health issues, studio counts) for every record. Records exist for Minecraft (reference), Terraria / Valheim / Zomboid (retro-fit, template) and the on-hold Hytale and FiveM/RedM.

**Staying current.** Lessons learned are appended to `docs/cyrus/onboarding/LESSONS.md` after every onboarding; rule changes bump `PLAYBOOK_VERSION` + `CHANGELOG.md`. Test: `test/cyrus-onboarding.test.ts` (ladder, health over every record, manifest, parser, docs coverage of the playbook, scaffolder end to end with type-check and clean-up).
EOF
tail -3 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md | cut -c1-80

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.
